title: Adaptive Neuron Networks for Predictive Modeling
abstract: This paper introduces a novel predictive modeling framework based on adaptive neuron networks. Traditional approaches often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting the model's flexibility. We propose an algorithm that leverages the inherent self-adaptative properties of neural networks to achieve more accurate predictions. The core mechanism involves utilizing a dynamically adjusted network architecture to represent and predict system behavior. This approach offers improved generalization and robustness compared to existing methods. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this framework through a series of quantitative and qualitative analyses, showcasing its ability to accurately predict complex dynamic systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications and future research directions.

title: 拓扑信息论的量子化结构
abstract: This paper explores the integration of topology into quantum information processing, proposing a novel computational framework centered around a quantum system governed by topological structures. We outline a design for a quantum computation engine leveraging self-correlation within quantum states, guided by topological principles to enhance algorithm efficiency. The core claim is that this approach offers a pathway toward exceeding the limitations of classical quantum computation by introducing a fundamentally new computational paradigm. The research delves into the potential of utilizing topological properties to guide quantum process execution, thereby facilitating the development of complex algorithms with improved performance. This work seeks to establish a theoretical foundation for quantum computation by integrating topology as a core design element.

title: Development and evaluation of an AI-powered conversational agent for small and medium enterprises
abstract: Цель исследования — сделать передовые аналитические инструменты доступными для предприятий малого и среднего бизнеса в сфере электронной коммерции. Для этого были определены аналитические функции, оказывающие наибольшее влияние на эффективность платформ, и разработана доступная система поддержки принятия решений на базе диалогового искусственного интеллекта (ИИ), предназначенная для пользователей без технической подготовки. Исследование проводилось на основе вторичных панельных данных четырех платформ электронной коммерции (Amazon, eBay, Shopify, Flipkart) и семи общедоступных наборов данных. Методы исследования: множественный регрессионный и корреляционный анализ показателей эффективности платформ; методология Design Science Research (исследование через проектирование) для разработки системы; тестирование юзабилити с использованием шкалы System Usability Scale (SUS). Основные результаты: в ходе кросс-платформенного анализа пяти гипотез (H1–H5) выявлена ​​наиболее сильная связь между рекомендациями ИИ и конверсией; разработана диалоговая ИИ-система с двумя режимами работы (на основе правил и с использованием API Claude); оценка системы десятью участниками показала средний балл SUS, равный 71,25, что соответствует целевому показателю приемлемости. Научная новизна заключается в проведении первой оценки на уровне пользователей аналитической системы с диалоговым ИИ, спроектированной и протестированной специально для целевой аудитории — сотрудников малых и средних предприятий электронной коммерции, не обладающих технической квалификацией. Выводы. Задачи диссертационного исследования решены, цель достигнута, а полученные результаты обладают признаками научной новизны.

title: Humans Teaching Machine Learning Agents
abstract: This chapter describes how nonexpert humans can train reinforcement learning (RL) agents. There are numerous ways to learn from human instruction – some have been studied more than others since this is an open field of research. A traditional machine learning approach focuses on the objective performance of the RL agent, optimizing metrics such as training time and reward. Verifying these RL systems is often done with simulated rather than real human input. We believe that to be a limiting approach. In this chapter, we will show: (1) a few methods of humans teaching RL agents; (2) how a great deal of information can be learned from testing these agents with human-subject studies; and (3) how objective performance does not need to be sacrificed in order to create a positive user experience. We can create a much better interactive machine learning system when designing and verifying from a human-centered perspective. We’ll cover different teaching methods, including advice and critique, and how they impact the user experience and objective performance of the agent. We’ll also discus how teaching methods are impacted by many factors, such as rhetorical arguments, immediacy of feedback, and issues of language processing. We’ll also cover a three-step process for the design and verification of interactive machine learning algorithms, and recommendations to improve the human experience.

title: Distilled Continuous Diffusion Language Models Can Write Code in Few Steps---or One
abstract: Language generation is almost universally treated as a sequential process: autoregressive models emit one token at a time, while diffusion language models replace token-level seriality with a long trajectory of iterative refinement. In this work, we introduce PlaidQ, a 0.7B continuous diffusion language model for code generation, and show that its trajectory can be aggressively distilled into only a few denoising steps---or even one, enabling efficient code generation. PlaidQ repurposes a pretrained autoregressive model as a bidirectional denoiser over continuous token embeddings. We distill PlaidQ with distribution matching for few-step generation and paired-trajectory supervision for one-step generation. At matched model scale, PlaidQ is competitive with discrete diffusion language models on code generation. Distillation then shifts the quality--compute frontier: a 16-step student reaches 31.78 and 40.49 pass@10 on HumanEval and MBPP+, surpassing the same PlaidQ teacher sampled for 512 steps. At the extreme, paired-trajectory distillation achieves 7.07 pass@1 on HumanEval with a single denoising step, producing functionally correct programs. Together, these results establish continuous diffusion as a viable path to few-step and one-step code generation. Broadly, continuous diffusion is not merely another representation for language: it provides an interface through which language models can inherit the acceleration and distillation machinery of continuous diffusion modeling. Training and inference code and model checkpoints are available at https://github.com/pengzhangzhi/plaidq.

title: Joint Alignment and Distillation for Video Generation via Sample-Guided Distribution Matching
abstract: Aligning video generative models to human preferences heavily relies on Reinforcement Learning (RL), which suffers from extensive computational overhead. Existing workflows typically treat RL and distillation as disconnected stages: applying RL before distillation incurs prohibitive computational costs, whereas applying RL after distillation frequently leads to model collapse. To overcome these limitations, we propose a unified, single-stage optimization framework grounded in Distribution Matching (DM). In the standard DM framework, distillation updates the model via a gradient direction that minimizes the gap between the real and fake models, guiding generations toward clarity and high fidelity. Building upon this, we introduce DM-Align, which derives a complementary gradient direction to guide the model toward human-preferred samples. Inspired by DPO and GRPO, our method leverages the distributional gap -- formulated from either preference pairs or intra-group exploration -- to directly construct this preference-guided gradient. By synergizing these two gradient directions, our approach eliminates the need for multi-step reward evaluation and complex ODE-SDE conversions inherent in traditional RL. Comprehensive experiments across multiple foundational video models demonstrate that this sample-guided framework robustly enhances both distillation quality and preference alignment, consistently outperforming both standalone variants and sequential two-stage pipelines.

title: KhatianDoc: A Human-Verified Benchmark Diagnosing Multimodal LLM Failure on Bengali Legal Land Records
abstract: Land ownership in Bangladesh is recorded in Ana-Ganda-Kora-Kranti-Til, a base-16 positional fraction system with dedicated Unicode glyphs, no mainstream font, and no coverage in any OCR pipeline or tokenizer. The handwritten records that carry these fractions, RS Khatians, are the authoritative title record for millions of parcels and a frequent subject of civil litigation, yet no benchmark has asked whether a machine can read one. We introduce KhatianDoc, a four-task benchmark built from 107 real RS Khatian records from the Vumi (land) Office of Munshiganj, Bangladesh: symbol recognition, base-16-to-decimal conversion, structured field extraction, and legal document question answering over 1,634 QA pairs. Ground truth was transcribed by hand, verified by a land-law practitioner to full agreement, and anonymized through positional tokens that keep the referential distinctions multi-hop questions depend on. We evaluate six multimodal LLMs (8B to 72B+, open and closed) under a fixed zero-shot protocol. Five QA categories, 39.3% of our stratified set, return zero correct answers from every model; on the arithmetic task, every model that emits a number does worse than a constant-mean baseline, with exact- and near-match scores coinciding: decorrelation, not approximation. Auditing our own metrics surfaced two artifacts in opposite directions: we correct a refusal-scoring bug and report the fixed scores beside the originals, and flag an inflated metadata metric as an upper bound. KhatianDoc documents not a performance gap but the absence of a capability, with verified ground truth for future systems. Code and data, with a redacted image release, are publicly available.

title: Natural Language Processing(NLP) : Techniques, Applications, and Challenges
abstract: This research paper provides an overview of Natural Language Processing (NLP), its key techniques, applications, and challenges. It explores methods such as text classification, sentiment analysis, machine translation, and language modeling, along with modern AI and Transformer-based approaches. The paper also discusses NLP limitations, including ambiguity, bias, multilingual processing, and context understanding.

title: Moving Target Defense (MTD) in Enterprise Endpoint Security Comparative Analysis with EDR/XDR and Market Adoption Assessment
abstract: Abstract: Moving Target Defence (MTD) represents a paradigm shift from reactive detection to proactive disruption in cybersecurity. Unlike traditional Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) or Extended Detection and Response (XDR) systems that rely on behavioural analysis and signatures, MTD dynamically alters system attack surfaces to invalidate adversary reconnaissance and exploitation. This paper provides a systematic comparison of MTD and EDR/XDR capabilities, identifying distinct advantages of MTD that current XDR implementations cannot replicate. We clarify that MTD complements rather than replaces XDR, as MTD lacks detection, remediation, and forensic capabilities. We conclude with deployment recommendations and a proposed stack combining MTD as a proactive prevention layer with existing XDR for response. title: The Dynamic Geometric Parameter Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometric parameter optimization algorithm designed to enhance the performance and reliability of optimization processes. Traditional optimization methods are often static, failing to adapt to the specific characteristics of the input data. Our algorithm leverages a dynamically adjusted parameter set, continuously refining its parameters based on real-time analysis to achieve optimal results. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing significant improvements in convergence speed and solution quality compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers on a feedback loop that monitors input data and adjusts parameter values in a statistically-informed manner.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Parallel Processing
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two particles become linked and share the same fate regardless of the distance separating them, holds immense potential for revolutionizing parallel processing. This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to establish parallel processing pathways across vast computational distances, aiming to enhance processing speed for complex calculations. We introduce a novel algorithm, the 'Entanglement Resonance' method, designed to leverage this phenomenon for efficient data transfer and accelerated computation. The core mechanism centers around establishing entangled states to facilitate information transfer and ultimately, improve performance. This research delves into the theoretical foundations, algorithm implementation, and potential practical applications of this approach, offering a pathway toward significantly faster computations for computationally intensive tasks.

title: 基于自适应量子势的机器学习算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning algorithm based on adaptive quantum potentials. Traditional machine learning often relies on manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and suboptimal. We propose a new approach where the quantum potential itself is dynamically adjusted during the training process, leading to improved model accuracy and enhanced quantum machine learning capabilities. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning quantum potential landscape, allowing the algorithm to automatically optimize the interaction between data and the quantum system. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of benchmark datasets and analysis of its performance compared to existing methods. This work introduces a fundamentally new paradigm in quantum machine learning, offering a potential pathway to more efficient and accurate quantum computations.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Adaptive Machine Learning Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive machine learning framework based on dynamic topology. Traditional machine learning algorithms often struggle with complex data due to their static nature. This framework leverages the unique properties of dynamic topology to dynamically adjust model parameters, thereby enhancing prediction accuracy and model generalization. We present a method for optimizing the model's parameters using a dynamically evolving topology, enabling adaptive strategies that respond to data variations and improve model performance. The core mechanism involves iterative refinement of the model's topology through a process of "folding" and "unfolding," leading to a more robust and adaptable learning process. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the framework's design, implementation, and evaluation, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of static models and achieve superior results in various machine learning applications.

Traditional machine learning algorithms often struggle with complex data due to their static nature. This framework leverages the unique properties of dynamic topology to dynamically adjust model parameters, thereby enhancing prediction accuracy and model generalization. We present a method for optimizing the model's parameters using a dynamically evolving topology, enabling adaptive strategies that respond to data variations and improve model performance. The core mechanism involves iterative refinement of the model's topology through a process of "folding" and "unfolding," leading to a more robust and adaptable learning process. This paper provides a comprehensive overview of the framework's design, implementation, and evaluation, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of static models and achieve superior results in various machine learning applications.

title: A Cognitive Architecture-Based General Artificial Intelligence Model
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to developing General Artificial Intelligence (GAI) by leveraging cognitive architectures. The core idea is to model human cognition—encompassing perception, memory, reasoning, learning, and decision-making—within a computational framework. This architecture is built upon a modular design, integrating deep learning and reinforcement learning techniques to enable the system to acquire and utilize diverse cognitive abilities. We argue that this approach, rooted in cognitive architecture, offers a more biologically plausible and potentially more effective path toward achieving true GAI compared to traditional, monolithic AI systems. The presented model aims to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and human intelligence, ultimately leading to a system capable of adapting and solving complex problems across various domains. This document details the architecture, key mechanisms, and anticipated advancements within this framework. ---

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Topology-Based Quantum Field Theory
abstract: This paper explores the concept of a dynamically generated topology-based quantum field theory, aiming to address limitations in current theoretical frameworks regarding entanglement and the nature of quantum information. The core mechanism involves an iterative algorithm that constructs topology features based on the evolving quantum state, offering a novel pathway to understanding quantum entanglement. We detail the theoretical underpinnings, the implementation of a quantum algorithm, and the potential implications for advancing our understanding of fundamental physics. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future research directions.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子系统动力学
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology to quantum system dynamics, aiming to enhance the simulation of quantum systems through dynamic topology. We propose a novel modeling approach that leverages the instantaneous changes inherent in dynamic topology to simulate quantum system evolution, offering a potential pathway towards more efficient quantum system design. Traditional approaches often struggle with complex systems, necessitating a shift towards dynamically evolving models. This work explores the potential of this technique, focusing on the core mechanism of simulating dynamic evolution through the application of transient topology. The paper introduces a framework for constructing a quantum system model based on adaptive topology, demonstrating its efficacy in simulating key quantum phenomena.

title: Hierarchical Graph Neural Networks for Semantic Landscape Construction
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic landscape construction utilizing Hierarchical Graph Neural Networks (HGNNs). Traditional methods often struggle to effectively represent and learn complex, multi-level semantic relationships inherent in landscape data. Our HGNN architecture addresses this limitation by decomposing the knowledge space into progressively abstract layers, enabling the capture of deep semantic hierarchies. The core mechanism involves a multi-level Graph Neural Network (GNN) where lower levels focus on capturing local graph structures, while higher levels learn abstract, compositional representations of the landscape. This approach significantly improves learning efficiency and allows for a more robust and accurate modeling of semantic landscapes compared to flat graph representations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a theoretical analysis and outline its potential applications in various domains, including environmental modeling, urban planning, and geographic information systems.

title: 基于自适应的量子算法的拓扑结构优化
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, and the development of efficient quantum algorithms is paramount to realizing its full potential. Current quantum algorithms often rely on fixed parameter configurations, limiting their ability to exploit subtle variations in the quantum state. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing a self-adaptive quantum algorithm to dynamically optimize the topology of quantum states, aiming to significantly enhance the performance of quantum computations. We propose a method based on iterative adjustments to the quantum state's geometry, guided by the inherent properties of the qubit system. This research focuses on establishing a robust and effective mechanism for automatic topology optimization, addressing the limitations of traditional approaches. The core claim is that this self-adaptive algorithm can significantly improve quantum computation efficiency through precise and automated topology manipulation. We detail the proposed algorithm, its underlying principles, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its efficacy. The significance of this work lies in its potential to unlock new levels of quantum algorithm performance by proactively tailoring the quantum state.

title: Fractal Dimension Scaling for Data Clustering
abstract: This paper proposes a novel clustering algorithm, Fractal Dimension Scaling (FDS), that leverages fractal dimension to enhance the representation of complex data distributions. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with data exhibiting non-linear, high-dimensional, and intricate patterns. FDS employs a fractal dimension metric to dynamically adjust the representation of data points, allowing the algorithm to better capture these complex characteristics. The paper details the theoretical framework underpinning FDS, including the mathematical formulation of the fractal dimension calculation and the implementation of a robust clustering process. We present a comparative analysis of FDS with established clustering techniques, demonstrating its superior ability to handle data with high dimensionality and non-linear relationships. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential applications of this algorithm across diverse data analysis domains. The primary focus is on the enhanced representation achieved by fractal dimension, leading to improved clustering outcomes.

title: ##基于神经符号的程序合成框架
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for program synthesis leveraging the synergy between deep learning and neuro-symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to automatically generate program code capable of solving specific problems, moving beyond simple code imitation. This is achieved through a multi-modal neural network that integrates feature extraction from input data with the construction and reasoning of neuro-symbolic representations. A "translator" component then converts these symbolic representations into executable code. The framework's ability to handle complex and abstract problem domains, coupled with its learning capability for efficient solutions, distinguishes it from existing program synthesis approaches that typically rely on constrained search spaces or predefined rules. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical exploration and outline a comprehensive architecture for future development. ---

title: Quantum Optimization for Adaptive Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable storage and manipulation of quantum information. Current quantum error correction codes, however, often rely on pre-defined parameters that may not optimally adapt to the specific characteristics of the quantum system being protected. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum error correction algorithm, designed to dynamically adjust error correction parameters based on the quantum system's inherent properties. We propose a quantum optimization algorithm that iteratively refines these parameters, leading to improved fidelity, stability, and overall performance. This work represents a significant advancement in error correction, offering a potential pathway towards more robust and versatile quantum systems.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Causal Inference – Bayesian Structural Causal Models (BSCMs)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal inference leveraging probabilistic programming and Bayesian Structural Causal Models (BSCMs). Traditional methods often struggle with the complexity of representing and reasoning about causal relationships, particularly in scenarios involving dynamic systems and counterfactual questions. We propose a probabilistic programming language designed to natively support BSCMs, offering a more flexible and expressive framework for causal modeling. This allows for dynamic causal reasoning – the ability to update causal models based on observed data – and facilitates sophisticated counterfactual analysis, enabling us to explore "what if" scenarios. The core contribution lies in integrating the strengths of probabilistic programming for model specification and Bayesian inference with the rigorous framework of BSCMs, providing a powerful tool for understanding and predicting causal effects. The language incorporates features for defining causal structures, specifying prior distributions, and performing inference using techniques like Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC). We demonstrate the potential of this approach through illustrative examples, highlighting its advantages over traditional methods.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Propagation for Robotics
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to enhance constraint propagation within robotics. Conventional constraint propagation algorithms struggle with complex environments, often requiring extensive simulations. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced technique that leverages quantum algorithms to efficiently explore potential trajectories and constraints, resulting in improved motion planning and robustness. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum annealing to accelerate the search for optimal solutions, leading to more efficient and robust motion planning. The research focuses on the potential of quantum computing to overcome the limitations of existing constraint propagation methods, specifically addressing challenges in dynamic environments and high-dimensional constraints. We present a preliminary analysis demonstrating improvements in planning efficiency and robustness compared to classical methods.

title: Green Edge AI: Constant-Time Memory Stabilization and Anomaly Preservation for Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Continuous ingestion of high-dimensional telemetry forces predictive networks into a severe space-time trade-off, where conventional outlier rejection algorithms dilute mathematical gradients with benign idle data and induce thermal throttling on local hardware. This study introduces an $\mathcal{O}(d)$ ternary quantized framework that autonomously segregates sequential telemetry into redundant cache, degradation envelopes, and adversarial noise using parameter-free interquartile scaling and peak density thresholds. Empirical evaluations utilizing empirical machining datasets verify that topological isolation definitively eliminates gradient explosions inherent to raw data ingestion. The architecture achieves empirical risk minimization four times faster than robust Z-score baselines by discarding uninformative payload mass, while entropy evaluations prove anomalous amputations induce negligible structural information loss. Hardware simulations validate an absolute thermodynamic equilibrium, entirely preventing processor thermal throttling. Isolating pure physical degradation signatures from bulk transmission fundamentally dismantles the dependency on logarithmic cloud-indexing for automated diagnostics. Resolving this computational bottleneck establishes a thermodynamically sustainable foundation for decentralized operations, strictly fulfilling global mandates for energy-efficient computing infrastructure without compromising predictive integrity.

abstract: Geometric topology provides a novel framework for Bayesian inference, addressing the challenges posed by complex data and the limitations of traditional methods. title: Enhanced Moss Growth Optimization with Benchmark Validation and a Wastewater Treatment Prediction Case Study
abstract: Complex optimization tasks in data-driven prediction and engineering applications often involve nonlinear, multimodal, and ill-conditioned objective functions. This study proposes an Enhanced Moss Growth Optimization algorithm (EMGO), an improved variant of the baseline MGO framework, to enhance exploratory step-size control and local covariance exploitation. EMGO incorporates two key algorithmic augmentations: a budget-adaptive jump regulation mechanism that balances global dispersal and fine-grained refinement, and a shrinkage-regularized covariance-guided sampling operator with relative eigenvalue flooring to exploit correlation structures among elite individuals without rank deficiency. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark suite across 50 and 100 dimensions with 29 test functions, 30 independent runs, and a budget of 3×105 function evaluations per run, compared against ten state-of-the-art optimizers including CMA-ES, L-SHADE, SBO, and baseline MGO. Nonparametric Friedman ranking, Holm-adjusted Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, and runtime-matched analyses demonstrate that EMGO achieves highly competitive performance across high-dimensional landscapes. Furthermore, EMGO is applied to tune support vector regression (SVR) hyperparameters for effluent suspended solid (SS) prediction using the UCI Water Treatment Plant dataset under an expanding-window rolling-origin cross-validation scheme. EMGO-SVR achieves superior predictive accuracy (RMSE=5.58±0.64, MAE=3.97±0.46, R2=0.889±0.028), outperforming standard SVR, tree-based ensembles, and Bayesian optimization baselines. SHAP-based feature importance analysis confirms the physical and process consistency of the model predictions.

title: An Energy-Based Conservative-Dissipative Latent Neural Evolution Operator for Magnetization Dynamics
abstract: We develop an energy-based reduced-order model for micromagnetic magnetization dynamics that couples a convolutional autoencoder to a structured latent neural ordinary differential equation. Motivated by the precessional-dissipative structure of the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation, the latent vector field is generated from the gradient of a learned scalar potential through an antisymmetric operator and a symmetric positive-semidefinite dissipative operator. This potential is learned in nonunique latent coordinates and is not identified with the Gibbs free energy, but decreases monotonically along autonomous continuous-time solutions, while the antisymmetric component permits motion along its level sets. The encoder, decoder, latent energy, and operators are trained jointly on short trajectory windows using latent and decoded-rollout losses alone, without time-derivative supervision, physical-energy labels, or dissipation penalties. At inference, an initial state is encoded once, evolved in latent space, and decoded only at the requested output times, enabling substantially cheaper trajectory prediction than the micromagnetic solver used to generate the training data. We compare quadratic, deep, and additive deep-quadratic latent energies on two datasets parameterized by field amplitude and generated for the two applied-field directions of the NIST $μ$MAG Standard Problem 4. Dissipative-only and antisymmetric-dissipative models achieve comparable accuracy on short training-style windows but differ substantially on uninterrupted rollouts, for which the antisymmetric-dissipative models provide markedly more accurate trajectory predictions. The deep-quadratic energy gives the best overall accuracy for both field directions and exhibits slower error growth when rollouts are extended to twice the training horizon.

title: Zero-Shot Novel Depth Synthesis Using 3D Foundation Models Scene Representations
abstract: 3D Foundation Models (3DFMs) such as VGGT have recently pushed the boundaries of 3D vision by predicting rich unified representations with feed-foward transformers. The scene representations learned by these models enable strong performance on multiple 3D vision tasks. In this paper, we investigate using their internal representations to infer 3D in the scene from new views. Our hypothesis is that in order to solve the task of 3D reconstruction, these models need to learn a representation that includes a large amount of general knowledge about 3D scenes. After showing that it is possible to decode hidden surfaces from internal 3DFM representations, we propose a method, Z3D, that estimates pointmaps in unseen views by doing latent diffusion on 3DFM representation. We show that Z3D can predict realistic depth maps for new views across multiple datasets.

In this paper, we investigate using their internal representations to infer 3D in the scene from new views. Our hypothesis is that in order to solve the task of 3D reconstruction, these models need to learn a representation that includes a large amount of general knowledge about 3D scenes. After showing that it is possible to decode hidden surfaces from internal 3DFM representations, we propose a method, Z3D, that estimates pointmaps in unseen views by doing latent diffusion on 3DFM representation. We show that Z3D can predict realistic depth maps for new views across multiple datasets.

title: Bioinfoysis Technical Report
abstract: Large language model agents have shown promise in bioinformatics, but most existing systems focus primarily on producing final answers, treating planning, tool use, and code execution as transient interactions. This design is poorly suited to long-horizon bioinformatics tasks, where conclusions must remain connected to the data, computations, and intermediate evidence that support them. We introduce \textbf{Bioinfoysis}, a multi-agent harness that represents each request as a persistent, artifact-grounded analysis run. Bioinfoysis combines global planning with step-wise, evidence-driven replanning: the planner maintains an executable checklist and revises pending steps using structured handoffs returned after each worker execution. These handoffs bind intermediate results to their responsible agent, checklist step, and plan generation, preventing stale evidence from being silently reused after replanning. A controlled runtime validates generated scripts, tables, and figures before they are used in downstream analysis or reporting, while role-specific context, persistent memory, and governed bioinformatics skills support reliable execution over long analysis trajectories. We evaluate Bioinfoysis on BixBench and two question-answering tracks of LAB-Bench 2. On BixBench, Bioinfoysis achieves state-of-the-art accuracy of 82.4\%. Across four underlying language models, Bioinfoysis increases average accuracy from 27.81\% to 64.13\% on SeqQA2 and from 3.13\% to 31.25\% on DbQA2. These results demonstrate that reliable bioinformatics automation depends not only on model capability, but also on the harness that governs planning, execution, memory, and evidence flow. We hope that the emergence of Bioinfoysis will play a driving and leading role in the development of the bioinformatics community. Our demo website can be seen in https://report.bioinfoysis.com/.

title: Selective Forgetting in LLMs
abstract: Executive Summary This work approaches the problem of selectively forgetting knowledge from a large language model (LLM) for the purposes of safety, copyright, security, or otherwise. Also known as machine unlearning, this entails training a model to forget certain elements of the dataset on which it was trained. Unlearning methods must be evaluated both in terms of the extent to which the information has successfully been forgotten, and the performance of the unlearned model on the remaining (retained) data. We build on the work of TOFU (Task of Fictitious Unlearning) [21], which provides a dataset and benchmark for evaluating unlearning techniques. We create a new, TOFU-inspired question–answer dataset for the task of machine unlearning. The new dataset includes 10,500 question–answer pairs relating to over 1,000 distinct, synthetic entities of several types. Each question–answer pair is tagged with the entities it refers to, with the graph representation of our dataset containing over 2,600 edges between different entities. We perform two experiments with our dataset. The first experiment aims to capture whether the difficulty of forgetting a concept from a LLM depends on its granularity. For example, is unlearning more likely to be successful if forgetting a single book, rather than the book's author (as an author is connected to multiple books)? We find that granularity does not have a tangible effect on model performance in our dataset. There may be a small effect from granularity on the difficulty of forgetting, but this is not statistically significant across our results. Our second experiment explores the knock-on effect of forgetting a relationship between two entities. For example, if unlearning has been run on a model to forget only who wrote a book, but not the book or author themselves, is the model worse at responding to other questions about that book or author? We find that the model performance is lower on questions that contain the entities pertained in the relationship, than on those that do not. 1

title: This dataset supports the paper "Cardinality-Adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Variable-Scale Cooperative Aerial Games"
abstract: This dataset supports the paper "Cardinality-Adaptive Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Variable-Scale Cooperative Aerial Games" (submitted to Applied Intelligence). It contains the complete training and evaluation records of CA-MAPPO, a cardinality-adaptive multi-agent proximal policy optimization algorithm for variable-scale cooperative aerial-game formations, generated with the JSBSim six-degree-of-freedom flight-dynamics engine in the loop.The dataset includes: (1) per-iteration training logs (episode return, periodic win rate, policy/value losses, entropy, KL divergence; JSONL) from three-seed main training runs and the gated three-stage curriculum (single-scale consolidation at 2v2, mixed-scale main stage on {2v2, 3v3, 5v5}, and ace-weighted final consolidation), covering trained scales and strictly held-out zero-shot scales {4v4, 6v6}; (2) paired evaluation results (win/draw/loss counts with Wilson confidence intervals; JSON) for CA-MAPPO, MAPPO, QMIX and ablation variants, organized by opponent level (L1–L4) × team size under a common-random-number protocol with 20 episodes per cell, plus zero-shot extrapolation evaluations at 10v10, 14v14 and 20v20; (3) ablation study data (without geometric attention bias, without set-attention critic, single-scale training, without per-scale advantage normalization, without win-rate-gated curriculum, UPDeT-faithful adaptation, and double-budget controls); (4) full-episode step-by-step simulation records (per-step state, hybrid action, reward, termination flag, and flight parameters for every agent); (5) automated maneuver-detector statistics behind the emergent-tactics analysis and self-attention weight maps (NPZ) behind the attention-analysis figures.The dataset contains raw data only — no figures, no plotted curves, no trained model weights.

title: Dynamic Geometry Adjustment in Probability Logic Models
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometry adjustment framework for probability logic models. The core idea is to dynamically adjust model parameters based on the input data's geometric complexity, optimizing model performance through this adaptive control. We propose a system that iteratively evaluates the model's performance against a defined metric, and then adjusts the parameters to minimize this metric. The framework leverages a geometric complexity measure derived from the input data, providing a robust and adaptable approach to parameter optimization. The paper details the model's architecture, training procedure, and performance evaluation, demonstrating its effectiveness in a range of scenarios. The focus is on creating a method that can automatically tune model parameters to achieve optimal performance.

title: Quantum Hidden Matrix
abstract: Quantum Hidden Matrix (QHM) is a novel approach to linear algebra computation leveraging quantum mechanics and the concept of quantum entanglement. This paper explores the potential of QHM to significantly accelerate linear algebra operations and enhance the capture of quantum entanglement, offering a potential paradigm shift in computational efficiency and accuracy. The core claim is that by utilizing quantum entanglement to manipulate and accelerate linear algebra calculations, we can achieve a substantial improvement over classical methods, particularly in scenarios involving complex calculations and sensitive data.

title: Quantum-Inspired Geometry for Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum-inspired geometry, a novel approach to pattern recognition, leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to design geometric structures with enhanced sensitivity to subtle patterns. This paper explores the integration of quantum concepts, such as superposition and entanglement, into the core design of geometric elements, aiming to improve pattern identification capabilities across diverse data types. We propose a new framework for geometric analysis, focusing on the creation of structures capable of capturing complex, non-linear relationships inherent in many real-world patterns. The research delves into the mathematical foundations of these structures, demonstrating their potential to surpass traditional methods in identifying nuanced distinctions. This work presents a preliminary investigation into the application of quantum-inspired geometry to pattern recognition, outlining a potential pathway toward more robust and adaptable pattern detection systems.

title: Quantum Information Evolution: An Adaptive Self-Assembly Approach
abstract: This paper investigates the evolution of quantum information through a novel self-adaptive quantum evolution model. We propose a framework that decomposes quantum states into multiple sub-states, dynamically adjusts these sub-states' interactions, and generates complex quantum states. The core mechanism centers on a "quantum self-assembly" process, enabling the system to evolve in response to environmental changes and specific goals. This approach surpasses traditional quantum computing by offering dynamic state adjustments and the ability to create more advanced quantum functionalities. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this model in generating complex quantum states through a tailored, self-regulated evolution process.

title: 基于自适应混沌的概率几何优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Chaotic Probability Optimization" (ACPO), based on the principles of self-adaptive chaos. Traditional optimization methods often require manual parameter tuning, which is ineffective for complex problems. ACPO leverages the inherent dynamics of chaotic systems to dynamically adjust optimization parameters, enabling the algorithm to discover more robust and globally optimal solutions. This research explores the potential of using self-adaptive chaos to overcome limitations inherent in conventional optimization techniques. We present a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, its performance characteristics, and its implications for various optimization challenges.

title: Title: Resonance-Based Dynamic Algorithm (RBD)
abstract: The optimization of dynamic algorithms is a complex challenge, often requiring iterative adjustments to parameters to achieve desired performance. Traditional optimization methods can be computationally expensive and may not always converge to optimal solutions. This paper introduces Resonance-Based Dynamic Algorithm (RBD), a novel algorithm that utilizes resonant principles to dynamically adjust parameters, thereby maximizing stability and efficiency. The core mechanism of RBD involves the development of a 'resonance matrix' that continuously monitors the system's state and automatically adjusts parameters to maintain optimal performance. This approach offers a fundamentally different paradigm for optimization, potentially leading to significant improvements in algorithm efficiency and stability. The paper details the algorithm's implementation, demonstrates its effectiveness through several illustrative examples, and discusses its potential implications for various dynamic algorithm applications.

title: Quantum Error Correction Coding and Feedback Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) that integrates coding with feedback control. The core idea is to leverage multi-particle error-correcting codes and dynamically calibrate individual qubits based on measurement outcomes. This synergistic combination aims to significantly enhance error correction efficiency and achieve high fidelity quantum information transmission. The proposed framework addresses the critical challenge of environmental noise-induced decoherence, a major impediment to practical quantum computation and communication. We outline the design principles, key formulas, and the underlying mechanisms driving this approach. Specifically, we detail the application of a specific concatenated code structure and introduce a control system that utilizes feedback loops to counteract identified errors. The effectiveness of this combined approach is discussed theoretically, highlighting the potential for improved error correction rates and robustness against various noise models.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm Design (QEAD)
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unparalleled computational speed and accuracy. This paper investigates the design of a novel algorithm, Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm Design (QEAD), that leverages entanglement to accelerate computation and enhance the analysis of complex data. We propose a 'Quantum Resonance' algorithm, a process that utilizes entanglement to rapidly traverse the state space, identifying patterns and correlations efficiently. The core mechanism of QEAD centers around exploiting entanglement to achieve significant speedups in data processing and simulation tasks. This work explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of QEAD, focusing on its potential to revolutionize areas demanding intricate data analysis.

title: Symbiotic Quantum-Classical Hybrid Learning for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel symbiotic learning framework that synergistically integrates quantum computing and classical reinforcement learning (RL). The core idea is to leverage the unique capabilities of quantum systems – specifically, their ability to efficiently represent and explore high-dimensional state spaces – alongside the established strengths of classical RL algorithms for policy optimization. We introduce a hybrid architecture where a quantum neural network (QNN) acts as a sophisticated state processor, generating candidate actions based on the current state, while a classical RL agent learns to refine and select the optimal actions. Our approach moves beyond quantum-inspired algorithms by establishing a genuine symbiotic relationship between quantum and classical components, leading to potentially faster learning rates and improved performance in complex RL environments. The framework is described mathematically, outlining the key components and interactions. We present a detailed mathematical formulation of the system, highlighting the contributions of both the quantum and classical components. The efficacy of the system is conceptually discussed, focusing on the benefits of combining quantum exploration with classical policy learning. This paper lays the groundwork for future research in this rapidly evolving field.

title: Automated Theorem Proving via Evolutionary Algorithms for Strategy Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of evolutionary algorithms (EAs) to optimize the strategy employed within automated theorem provers (ATPs). Traditional ATPs often rely on pre-defined, static proof strategies, which can be inefficient for complex theorems. We propose a novel approach where an EA dynamically explores and adapts proof strategies, iteratively refining them based on their effectiveness in solving theorems. The core of our method involves encoding different proof strategies as individuals within an EA population, evaluating their performance using established ATP metrics (e.g., proof length, number of steps), and employing selection, mutation, and crossover operators to evolve the population towards strategies that consistently demonstrate superior proof performance. The results presented demonstrate the potential of this adaptive strategy optimization to significantly improve the efficiency and effectiveness of ATPs. We outline the key components of the system, including the EA implementation, the ATP interface, and the evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we discuss the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Societies of Narrow Minds: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Multi-Agent Systems and Emergent Cooperation in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of multi-agent and cooperation as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Quantum Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm (QTAOA) represents a novel approach to optimization, leveraging the unique properties of quantum topology to dynamically explore solution spaces and identify optimal configurations. This paper introduces a framework where the algorithm iteratively adjusts its search strategy based on feedback from a quantum-inspired probabilistic model, enabling automated discovery of optimal solutions across diverse application domains, particularly within machine learning and circuit design. This work offers a fundamentally different paradigm compared to traditional optimization methods, promising to address limitations in efficiency and robustness.

title: Quantum Simulation of Self-Adaptive Gradient Descent
abstract: Quantum simulation offers unprecedented capabilities for studying complex quantum systems, but traditional methods often struggle with computational complexity and require significant parameter adjustments. This paper introduces a novel quantum simulation approach utilizing self-adaptive gradient descent, a technique designed to dynamically adjust simulation parameters based on observed results. This algorithm significantly enhances simulation accuracy and efficiency by intelligently optimizing the simulation process. We present a framework that allows for continuous parameter refinement, mitigating the limitations of static parameter settings. The core mechanism centers around a learned parameter adjustment strategy, leveraging the inherent dynamics of the quantum system to improve the simulation. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, showcasing a substantial improvement in simulation fidelity compared to existing methods. The findings highlight the potential of self-adaptive gradient descent for accelerating and refining quantum simulations.

abstract: Quantum-enhanced diffusion is a novel approach to material characterization that leverages the principles of quantum mechanics to accelerate the diffusion process, resulting in significantly improved accuracy and speed compared to traditional methods. This paper introduces a new methodology centered around carefully engineered quantum states to manipulate the diffusion mechanism, leading to enhanced data acquisition and a more detailed understanding of material properties. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum tunneling to reduce noise and enhance the sensitivity of the measurement, ultimately enabling the precise characterization of diffusion processes. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this technique. This method offers a substantial advancement over existing techniques, promising a paradigm shift in the field of material science and engineering.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Constraint Satisfaction for Complex Constraint Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum computing principles to enhance constraint satisfaction problems (CSPs), specifically for complex, large-scale systems. We propose a novel quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction technique, utilizing quantum algorithms to expedite the search process and improve solution accuracy. The core mechanism centers on exploiting quantum properties – superposition and entanglement – to effectively explore the solution space and mitigate the exponential complexity inherent in traditional CSP solvers. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and potential benefits, demonstrating improved performance compared to classical methods on benchmark CSPs. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced constraint satisfaction can significantly reduce computational time and improve solution quality for complex systems, offering a substantial advancement in this field.

title: The intersection of post-quantum cryptography and QaaS: architecting quantum-safe cloud infrastructures
abstract: Introduction By 2030, an estimated 40% of current cloud infrastructures may be rendered vulnerable by cryptanalytically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs). Methods This paper introduces a 4-tier security framework tailored for Quantumas-a-Service (QaaS) deployments, focusing on securing data-in-transit. Integrating 3 NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLHDSA), our architecture mitigates interception threats based on Shor's algorithm. Results Emulation across an enterprise cloud topology demonstrates a maximum latency overhead of 17.7 milliseconds per TLS handshake under high-latency WAN conditions, ensuring high-availability operations without catastrophic fragmentation failure. Discussion The proposed model demonstrates the viability of modern latticebased cryptography for live environments and provides a structured 3-phase transition roadmap for cloud service providers (CSPs) to achieve quantum-resilience seamlessly.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence in detecting pulmonary nodules on computed tomography: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Objectives: Pulmonary nodules are frequent findings on chest computed tomography (CT) and are crucial for early lung cancer detection. Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), has emerged as a powerful tool for automated nodule detection, but diagnostic performance varies across studies. The objective of this study is to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of AI-based imaging systems in detecting pulmonary nodules on CT and compare DL with traditional computer-aided detection (CAD) and radiologists. Material and Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMADTA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched up to March 2025. Eligible studies assessed AI for pulmonary nodule detection on CT and reported sensitivity, specificity, or sufficient data for 2×2 contingency tables. Pooled estimates of sensitivity, specificity, and diagnostic odds ratio (DOR) were calculated using a bivariate random-effects model. Subgroup analyses examined DL versus CAD, detection of nodules <10 mm, and AI performance compared with radiologists. Study quality was evaluated using QUADAS-2. Results: Twenty-six studies comprising 31,742 CT scans were included. Pooled sensitivity and specificity of AI were 0.90 (95% CI 0.87–0.93) and 0.87 (95% CI 0.84–0.90), respectively, with a DOR of 60.2 and an area under the sROC curve of 0.94. DL outperformed CAD (sensitivity 0.92 vs 0.83; specificity 0.88 vs 0.84). Sensitivity for nodules <10 mm was lower (DL 0.82; CAD 0.68). AI matched radiologists, and AI-assisted radiologists showed improved sensitivity (0.93). Conclusion: AI demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy in pulmonary nodule detection, outperforming CAD and matching radiologists, with the greatest potential as a second reader in lung cancer screening.

title: Pemodelan Akustik HMM–GMM untuk Pengenalan Ucapan Kata Darurat Bahasa Indonesia
abstract: Keamanan dan keselamatan merupakan kebutuhan dasar manusia. Situasi darurat seperti pencurian, kebakaran, maupun ancaman lainnya sering kali memerlukan respons yang cepat untuk mengurangi dampak negatifnya. Seiring berkembangnya teknologi, sistem keamanan berbasis suara menjadi solusi potensial untuk meningkatkan efektivitas deteksi dini dan tanggapan terhadap keadaan darurat. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengembangkan model akustik berbasis Hidden Markov Model–Gaussian Mixture Model (HMM–GMM) guna mendeteksi kata-kata darurat dalam Bahasa Indonesia, seperti tolong, jangan, maling, kebakaran, dan kecelakaan. Dataset yang digunakan terdiri atas 1.100 berkas audio yang seimbang antara kelas darurat dan non-darurat. Fitur akustik dari dataset diekstraksi menggunakan Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) beserta fitur turunan delta dan delta-delta. Evaluasi dilakukan dengan metode 10-fold cross-validation dan model terbaik diujikan dengan data holdout test untuk memastikan kemampuan generalisasi model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa model HMM–GMM dengan 4 state dan 16 komponen Gaussian memberikan performa terbaik dengan akurasi 94,5%, presisi 94,3%, recall 94,5%, dan F1-score 94,4% pada hold. Temuan ini membuktikan bahwa model HMM–GMM efektif dalam mengenali ucapan darurat Bahasa Indonesia secara akurat dan efisien.

title: Разработка информационно-аналитического инструмента поддержки маркетинговых решений на основе аффинити-анализа и LLM-интерпретации пользовательских отзывов (на примере сети «Золотое Яблоко»)
abstract: Целью работы является разработка воспроизводимого инструмента, позволяющего на основе отзывов и связанной с ними поведенческой информации выявлять пересечения аудиторий бренда, анализировать тематическую структуру клиентского опыта и представлять результаты в прикладной форме. В работе использованы методы сбора и очистки открытых данных, аффинити-анализ, тематическая обработка текстов на основе эмбеддингов и кластеризации, LLM-интерпретация тематических групп и методы визуальной аналитики. В результате сформирована эмпирическая база по сети «Золотое Яблоко», реализованы алгоритмы расчета аффинити и интегрального показателя с учетом масштаба бренда, разработан процесс обработки отзывов и дашборд «Клиентский контур», объединяющий модули аффинити-анализа, геоаналитики и тематического сравнения. Результаты работы могут быть использованы в маркетинговой, CX- и конкурентной аналитике для выбора смежных брендов, локализации проблемных зон клиентского опыта и формирования гипотез для партнерств и локальных пилотов. Сделан вывод о том, что отзывы картографической платформы могут выступать системной основой для поддержки маркетинговых решений при условии их комплексной аналитической обработки.

title: Enhancing Deep Knowledge Tracing with Semantic Question Embeddings for Engineering Mathematics Education
abstract: In a course, with potentially up to hundreds of students, no instructor can guide each stu-dent’s learning process individually. Knowledge tracing is a technique that estimates what a student knows from their answers, and can be used to suggest what to practice next. Exist-ing methods treat each question as a single opaque number or requires hand-labelling each question with the concept it tests, and may need thousands of past student records before they work. A new course has none of this. This thesis proposes EmbeddingDKT, which represents each question by a language model’s embedding of its text, along with a pipeline that builds a question bank and simulated students for a new course from its syllabus alone (MATH 267, University Calculus II ). On real student data it ranks first among comparable models (AUC 0.833), scores questions it has never seen almost as well as familiar ones, and in simulation guides learners to their weakest topics faster than random practice.

title: Towards a universal language of concepts: A survey
abstract: Humans can learn and generalize novel concepts from sparse data because they express knowledge in rich structural formats. In this paper, we propose that programs are a strong candidate for universal representation of concepts. We review computational models of concept learning that use programs as their concept representation and evaluate their contribution toward a universal representational language.

title: GazeFS: Target-Centered Gaze-Trajectory Forecasting and Stabilization from Gaze-Head History
abstract: Target-centered gaze interaction requires more than suppressing frame-to-frame fluctuations: target acquisition produces task-aligned changes in gaze-head dynamics, while a gaze trace may retain a persistent target-relative residual direction. We formulate gaze correction as online target-centered gaze-trajectory forecasting and stabilization and introduce GazeFS, which maps a variable-length gaze-head history to the next target-center direction and a short-horizon Search/Focus estimate without target information at inference. Across 7,960 acquisition episodes from 30 participants, Search-Focus differences remain stable under quality control, onset exclusion, and duration matching. History windows improve phase decoding over the current endpoint, but explicit task progress remains a strong control. Under the 30-participant, five-fold grouped out-of-fold protocol across three seeds, the reductions relative to raw hold in Focus episode bias, within-episode dispersion, and P90 target error are 0.182 degrees, 0.257 degrees, and 0.400 degrees, with participant-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals excluding zero. Endpoint-free replay from empty history preserves the Focus advantage and yields raw-network phase balanced accuracy/AUPRC of 0.925/0.993; coordinate controls further show that recent history contributes beyond explicit progress metadata. GazeFS therefore improves Focus target centering and empirical residual contraction while leaving temporal smoothness as a separate objective.

title: LevelSyn: Physical-Aware Logic Synthesis via Level-Asynchronous Graph Neural Networks
abstract: As integrated circuit technology scales into the nanometer regime, the traditional disconnect between logic synthesis and physical design has led to significant PPA (Power, Performance, and Area) degradation and prolonged design closure cycles. Traditional logic synthesis relies on non-physical Wire Load Models (WLMs), while recent spectral-based placement predictors often neglect the inherent hierarchical logic depth and signal flow of netlists, which leads to low-fidelity spatial estimations. To bridge this gap, we propose LevelSyn, a novel physical-aware logic synthesis framework that integrates hierarchical representation learning with a wirelength-driven optimization engine. At its core, LevelSyn leverages a level-asynchronous Graph Neural Network (GNN) to predict high-fidelity gate coordinates by capturing the structural and directional semantics of And-Inverter Graphs (AIGs). To handle industrial-scale designs, a level-aligned subgraph partitioning strategy is introduced to eliminate memory bottlenecks while preserving local logical dependencies. These spatial insights are seamlessly integrated into a newly developed physical-informed synthesis engine within the Berkeley ABC framework. Experimental results on the EPFL benchmark suite demonstrate that LevelSyn significantly outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, achieving an average power reduction of 6.89\% and a timing delay improvement of 27.48\%. Furthermore, post-place-and-route validation shows a 99.59\% reduction in design rule check (DRC) violations, highlighting its effectiveness in accelerating design convergence.

title: Equidistant sets for additive kernels with finitely many negative squares
abstract: We isolate a linear-algebraic principle underlying several recent bounds for equilateral sets and equidistant codes. Let κ be a symmetric kernel on a set S that can be written as a squared Hilbert distance minus a squared distance into a space of dimension at most q (equivalently, an anchored Schoenberg kernel with at most q negative squares). For the coordinatewise sum of κ on Sn we prove that any m points whose pairwise kernel values all equal d > 0 satisfy R = (d/2)Cm + X with X positive semidefinite of rank at most qn, and consequently m ≤ 1 + Σt rt, where rt is the affine rank of the positive features of the alphabet actually used in coordinate t. A stable version replaces exactness by an operator-norm error and a spectral-tail budget. Three applications. (1) For codes in Zqn that are equidistant with respect to the squared Lee weight, |C| ≤ (q/2)n + 1 for even q and |C| ≤ 2⌈(q-1)/4⌉n + 1 for odd q, with no linearity assumption; for q = 5 the bound |C| ≤ 2n+1 is attained by an explicit evaluation code for every n = (5k-1)/2. (2) For p ∈ (4k, 4k+2) we recover the centred-Gram identity used by Ge–Xu–Zhou and tighten the finite negative rank budget from 4kn to 2kn; this rank improvement alone does not imply a linear cardinality bound. (3) The sharp first-order asymptotics of the Schütte problem on 2 ≤ p ≤ 4: limN N(Rp(N) - 1) = 2/p. Contents. Manuscript (PDF and LaTeX source) plus the two verification scripts covering every finite numerical claim, with a SHA-256 manifest. Both re-ran green on 2026-09-03. The proofs are analytic; the scripts check the finite claims, the closed forms and the negative controls. Status. Author preprint, not peer reviewed. A priority audit found no prior statement converting a negative-square count into an equilateral-set cardinality bound; scope was arXiv plus the reference lists of the cited works, with MathSciNet and zbMATH not searched. A finite search is not a proof of priority. Corrections welcome. AI disclosure. Anthropic Claude and OpenAI Codex were used as research tools for strategy exploration, derivation suggestions, symbolic and numerical checks, adversarial review, code drafting and manuscript drafting; the scripts were re-run in a separate session from the one that produced them. The author takes full responsibility for the accuracy and originality of the manuscript.

title: Adaptive Topology Quantum Computing Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing algorithm, termed Adaptive Topology Quantum Algorithm (ATQA), designed to address the challenges of large-scale geometric optimization problems. Traditional approaches often rely on classical optimization techniques, while ATQA leverages the principles of adaptive topology to achieve improved efficiency and accuracy. We detail the algorithm's core mechanism, the underlying theory behind the adaptive topology, and its potential for tackling complex geometric optimization tasks. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's implementation, performance evaluation, and future research directions.

title: Quantum Walk-Based Optimization of Reinforcement Learning Policies
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum walks to enhance the optimization of reinforcement learning (RL) policies. Traditional RL algorithms often struggle with exploring complex state spaces efficiently, leading to slow learning rates and suboptimal solutions. We propose a novel approach that leverages the inherent properties of quantum walks – superposition and interference – to accelerate the learning process. Specifically, we represent the RL environment as a graph and perform a quantum walk on this graph. The walk's quantum superposition allows for simultaneous exploration of multiple actions, drastically reducing the time required to converge to an optimal policy. We outline the theoretical framework, detailing the mathematical formulation of the quantum walk and its interaction with the RL environment. The core contribution lies in demonstrating how quantum walk's ability to explore multiple states concurrently can provide a significant advantage over classical approaches in optimizing RL policies. We present a conceptual model and a set of equations describing the process, highlighting the key elements for implementation. The results, while theoretical, demonstrate the feasibility and potential impact of this hybrid quantum-classical approach for tackling complex RL problems.

title: Symbolic Regression with Grammatical Evolution and Temporal Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for discovering mathematical relationships from data. However, it frequently faces challenges when dealing with time-series data, specifically capturing and enforcing temporal dependencies and constraints. This work introduces a novel approach that combines grammatical evolution, a genetic algorithm designed for program evolution, with temporal constraint propagation. The core idea is to guide the evolutionary process using rules that ensure the generated symbolic expressions adhere to the inherent temporal order present in the data. This integration leverages the generative capabilities of grammatical evolution while providing a mechanism for rigorous temporal reasoning. The proposed method offers a promising solution for accurately modeling complex time-dependent systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework outlining the core components and their interactions, focusing on the underlying mathematical principles.

title: Self-Referential Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Discovery
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to knowledge discovery within graphs by introducing Self-Referential Graph Neural Networks (SR-GNNs). Traditional Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) operate passively, learning representations based solely on the graph structure and node features. This limits their ability to adapt and refine their understanding, particularly in complex graph scenarios. Our core idea is to equip nodes within a GNN with the capability to directly influence the network's architecture and training process, establishing a feedback loop for iterative improvement. This allows the network to dynamically adjust its parameters, node embeddings, and even structural elements, ultimately leading to a more robust and accurate representation of the graph's underlying knowledge. The SR-GNN framework is designed to address the limitations of static GNNs by incorporating a self-reflective mechanism. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a theoretical analysis and outline the key components needed for implementation, highlighting its potential to significantly enhance knowledge discovery tasks within graph-structured data.

title: Quantum Error Correction: A Dynamic Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is a critical component of quantum computing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum information. Classical error correction relies on redundancy and error detection, which are fundamentally limited by the speed of light. Quantum error correction, however, offers the potential for significantly higher error rates and is intrinsically linked to the quantum state itself. This paper explores a novel dynamic adaptive algorithm for QEC, focusing on optimizing the quantum state representation and error correction process through a feedback mechanism. We demonstrate that this algorithm, designed specifically for QEC, achieves substantially improved precision and adaptability compared to existing approaches, offering a path towards more robust and efficient quantum systems. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting the quantum state to better respond to the effects of errors, leading to a significant enhancement in error correction capabilities.

title: Dynamic Adjustment of Multi-Qubit Error Correction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to multi-qubit error correction that dynamically adjusts its strategy based on real-time monitoring of the error correction environment. Traditional multi-qubit error correction schemes often employ fixed, pre-defined protocols, which may be suboptimal when faced with fluctuating noise levels or changing quantum system characteristics. We introduce a framework utilizing machine learning algorithms to continuously assess the error correction environment and adapt the correction strategy accordingly. This dynamic adjustment mechanism aims to improve correction efficiency and robustness by optimizing the correction process to the current conditions. The core claim of this work is the design of a system capable of adapting its error correction strategy dynamically, while the core mechanism relies on machine learning for real-time environmental monitoring and strategic adjustment. The potential impact of this approach is significant, particularly in the development of more reliable and scalable quantum computing architectures.

В данной работе была рассмотрена проблема потери актуальности словаря предметных концептов и текстовых шаблонов в системе ассоциативно-семантической поддержки принятия решений по данным беспилотных летательных аппаратов (БПЛА). Для решения этой проблемы был разработан метод статистического мониторинга актуальности, который позволяет автоматически выявлять семантический дрейф, деградацию концептов, пробелы в покрытии и появление новых смыслов в потоке наблюдений. Все расчеты проводились в программном обеспечении MS Office (Excel) и Colab.

title: PERTEK-ÇEMİŞGEZEK (TUNCELİ) HATTINDAKİ DEMİRLİ ZONLARIN ASTER VNIR-SWIR BANTLARI KULLANILARAK TESPİTİ
abstract: Çalışma alanı Pertek-Çemişgezek (Tunceli) hattında Keban Baraj Gölü’nün kuzeyinde yer alır. Bu zonda, magmatik birimlerle metamorfik birimlerin kontakları boyunca demirli cevher ve alterasyon ürünleri gelişmiştir. Bölgedeki ekonomik oluşuklar uzun yıllardır araştırmacıların dikkatini çekmektedir. Bu çalışmada mevcut alandaki potansiyel demirli zonların varlığının ve yayılımının uydu teknolojileri yoluyla tespiti hedeflenmiştir. Bu amaçla, Pertek-Çemişgezek (Tunceli) bölgesindeki, bilinen demirli zonlar referans alınarak ASTER uydusunun VNIR-SWIR bantları üzerinden görüntü zenginleştirme metotları uygulanmış ve kompozit görüntüler oluşturulmuştur. Saha gözlemlerinde hem mermerlerin hem de yan kayaların içerisinde ağsal ve yer yer masif cevherleşme izleri doğrulanmıştır. Sonuçta, literatür kaynaklı lokasyonlar, hem uydu gözlemleri hem de saha doğrulama çalışmaları ile tespit edilmiştir. Buna göre, Pertek-Çemişgezek (Tunceli) hattında; Ayazpınarı demir (Fe) zuhurları, Ballıdut FeOx Alterasyonları, Çemişgezek Elazığ Yol Yarması FeOx Alterasyonları şeklinde demirli ve demirce zengin zonlar tespit edilmiştir. Yapılan analizlerde en uygun RGB bant kombinasyonunun R: VNIR (Band 2 / Band 1), G: SWIR Band 6 ve B: VNIR Band 3 olduğu belirlenmiştir.

title: CT-based cross-center risk stratification of pure ground-glass nodules incorporating domain style–aware correction
abstract: BackgroundPure ground-glass nodules (pGGNs) are increasingly detected on chest CT. Although most exhibit indolent behavior, a subset may harbor invasive features before obvious radiological progression, making early risk stratification clinically important.PurposeTo develop and externally validate a CT-based deep learning model with domain adaptation for cross-center risk stratification of pGGNs.Material and MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included 1235 surgically confirmed pGGNs from two institutions. A deep learning model incorporating domain style-aware correction was developed to differentiate AAH/AIS-like lesions from MIA/IAC-like lesions using preoperative CT images. Data from one center were used for training and internal validation, and an independent external cohort was used for validation. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, accuracy, calibration, and decision curve analysis.ResultsThe model achieved an AUC of 0.93 and an accuracy of 90.4% in the internal validation set. In the external validation set, the AUC was 0.88 with an accuracy of 81.7%, demonstrating good cross-center generalization. Domain adaptation improved external AUC from 0.85 to 0.88. Calibration analysis showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. Decision curve analysis indicated higher net benefit compared with treat-all and treat-none strategies across a range of thresholds.ConclusionThe proposed model demonstrates robust performance across centers and may serve as a noninvasive tool to support individualized surveillance strategies for patients with pGGNs.
