title: Scale-QLoRA: Code-Invariant Adapter Merging for Native 4-bit Microscaling LLMs
abstract: Merging a LoRA adapter into its base model is standard deployment practice: it removes the runtime adapter's per-forward overhead and leaves a single standalone checkpoint any serving stack can load. On a native 4-bit microscaling checkpoint (NVFP4, MXFP4) that step stops being free. The merged weights must be written back through a quantizer, which re-derives the checkpoint's discrete E2M1 code plane (roughly 90% of the artifact's bytes), so the deployed artifact becomes coupled to one quantization convention, and every later code-touching event in its lifecycle can move it. Done naively the step is worse than fragile: it deletes the adaptation, by up to 39 pp, because against an already-on-grid base the reconstruction optimum is that base. Scale-QLoRA instead adapts only the native per-block scale field, trains those scales on the deployment grid, and freezes every E2M1 code. Within a fixed native format, scale grid, block layout and code plane, merging is then a bit-exact identity and the merged artifact is code-invariant. Across four models and four tasks, Scale-QLoRA and merge-aware QAT-LoRA are both accuracy-lossless, so we claim no accuracy ordering between them; they differ structurally, in that QAT-LoRA re-derives the code plane through a quantizer while Scale-QLoRA preserves it exactly. That difference is what the lifecycle prices: nearest-rounding implementations disagree by about a point on the measured task, and more extreme rule mismatches can drive the weight-space artifact to ~0%, which we report as a sensitivity bound rather than a deployment frequency. Preserving the code plane also drops the weight-space straight-through estimator from training (3.9x per step on the dense 8B model) and enables exact rollback, code-plane deduplication, and a ~125x faster scale-only task swap.

title: Adapting to Evolving Requirements: Agentic AI for Retail Supply Chain Operations
abstract: Retail supply chain operations rely on coupled decision modules that must adapt as requirements evolve. LLMs offer a natural-language interface for this task, but existing methods primarily focus on individual optimization models. Extending them to heterogeneous decision pipelines is challenging because a requirement may admit multiple intervention paths with different downstream effects. We formulate requirement-driven adaptation as the joint selection of an intervention route and an admissible module-level change, and propose a graph-constrained agentic framework in which domain agents expose admissible reformulation interfaces and a central processor searches over bounded intervention paths. Candidates are validated and compared using downstream KPIs. In collaboration with a large retail partner, we evaluate 100 warehouse requirements elicited from practitioner interviews, with GPT, Qwen, and DeepSeek as base LLMs. Relative to direct LLM reformulation, our framework improves correctness and end-to-end success across all three models, raising end-to-end success from 72--76% to 79--83%.

title: From Prior-Guided Heuristics to Deployable Agents: Accelerating Demonstration-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Deadline-Constrained Network Control
abstract: Timely delivery of delay-sensitive information over dynamic, heterogeneous networks is essential for NextG interactive applications, yet providing strict End-to-End (E2E) peak latency guarantees remains an open challenge. Two obstacles limit the adoption of learning-based network control in this setting: traditional volume-based routing metrics, while highly effective for general traffic management, are not designed to capture traffic urgency; and Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) controllers trained from scratch suffer from sample inefficiency, long training times, and early-stage exploration volatility. This paper introduces a deployment-focused network control framework that addresses both obstacles. First, we present Effective Congestion (EC), a deadline-aware metric family that quantifies interface congestion by packet urgency and proactively filters non-viable traffic, coupled with a Uniform Path Grouping (UPG) distribution heuristic promoting robust load-balancing; the resulting policies are embedded into Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Effective Congestion ($p^*$) (MADRL EC ($p^*$)), a hybrid architecture combining a distributed scheduler with a centralized RL-based router. Second, we introduce a unified training objective that generalizes existing policy-learning paradigms---behavioral cloning, offline Reinforcement Learning (RL), online RL, and offline-to-online schemes---as special cases, combining a live-reward term, a pre-collected-reward term, and a policy-imitation term. title: Time Without Timesteps: Simulating Coupled Dynamical Systems via Self-Consistency
abstract: Numerical simulation of dynamical systems is usually organized as a causal march through time: each state is computed from the previous one. We explore a different formulation for coupled systems. For each subsystem type we train a neural surrogate mapping a full driving trajectory and initial condition directly to a full output trajectory; following classical waveform relaxation, coupled systems are assembled by enforcing self-consistency among these trajectories: simulation becomes a fixed-point problem over complete trajectories rather than a stepwise rollout. On coupled van der Pol oscillators and Hodgkin-Huxley neuron networks, sequential depth becomes the number of solver iterations: 4-10 Newton iterations where the reference integrator takes 1500 steps. The gradient likewise loses its time recursion: it becomes a linear system solved by GMRES at memory independent of solver depth. A single scalar measured from the learned operator, the spectral radius of its Jacobian, predicts in advance where the coupled solve will converge; past that boundary, unrolled backpropagation diverges and a Neumann adjoint fails, while the implicit gradient remains correct to 0.04%. We report where the approach succeeds and where surrogate error degrades it.

title: Kovoluutioneuroverkot ja niiden käyttö rintasyövän havaitsemiseen mammografiakuvista
abstract: This bachelor's thesis discusses convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and their use in the detection of breast cancer from mammographic images. In addition, the thesis introduces six classic CNN architectures. The aim of the thesis is to gather information on the operation of CNNs, classic CNN architectures and the development of them, and the potential use of CNNs. The discussion of the potential use of CNNs focuses on the detection of breast cancer from mammographic images. The thesis was conducted as a literature review. CNNs are machine learning models that are particularly well-suited for the analysis of images. CNNs consist of layers that receive and transmit information using feature maps. In convolutional layers, maps obtained as input are processed using weighted filters and convolution. Each filter in a layer produces a feature map for the output of the layer. In pooling layers, the size of the feature maps decreases, as sections in the maps are replaced with averages or maximums, for example. The adjustable parameters of a network are updated during training using training data. In studies where the analysis of mammographic images has been tested using CNNs, the detection has often been implemented in two stages. First, the mammographic images are often segmented or preprocessed in other ways. In the second stage, CNNs classify the given images. In testings with human radiologists, the results of CNN models have been even better than the ones of individual radiologists. However, CNNs have difficulties in cases underrepresented in the training data. In a study where a hybrid of a CNN and a human radiologist was tested, the hybrid obtained better results than either of the parts individually. The results indicate that radiologists could benefit from using CNNs as help with the analysis of mammograms.

title: Geometric Predictive Modeling with Hybrid Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric predictive modeling approach leveraging hybrid neural networks and geometric data analysis. We address the challenge of accurately predicting complex geometric structures from data by integrating the strengths of both neural networks – adept at pattern recognition – and geometric analysis – capable of uncovering underlying structures and relationships. The proposed model employs a layered architecture, initially leveraging a convolutional neural network to extract initial features and then integrating a geometric regression module to refine these features and predict geometric properties. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness across a range of geometric datasets, achieving state-of-the-art predictive performance in several benchmark scenarios. The core mechanism centers on the synergistic interplay between these two computational paradigms, leading to enhanced predictive capabilities compared to traditional methods.

title: 基于量子纠缠的模式识别算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel pattern recognition algorithm leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The algorithm utilizes a quantum entanglement-based processing framework to enhance pattern identification and classification, specifically designed to effectively handle complex patterns often found within data. Traditional pattern recognition methods can be susceptible to noise, making them suboptimal for intricate datasets. Our proposed approach aims to overcome these limitations by exploiting the correlated nature of entangled particles, offering a potential paradigm shift in pattern analysis. The core mechanism centers around establishing and maintaining entanglement between data points, allowing for a more robust and efficient pattern recognition process. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying patterns within complex datasets.

title: Decoherence Times and Quantum Speed Limits in Spin-Chain Systems: A Many-Body Testbed for Energy-Time Uncertainty
abstract: Quantum speed limits (QSLs) constrain the minimum time for quantum state evolution, typically derived from energy bounds like the Margolus-Levitin (ML) and Mandelstam-Tamm (MT) relations. In open systems, decoherence—driven by environmental interactions—may impose additional constraints. This work investigates whether decoherence times fundamentally limit QSLs in spin-chain systems, extending ML/MT bounds to open dynamics. By modeling spin chains with Lindblad equations and simulating Heisenberg-type interactions, we analyze the interplay between energy fluctuations, decoherence rates, and evolution times. Experimental validation via trapped-ion or superconducting-qubit arrays could test energy-time uncertainty in many-body systems. Introduction Quantum speed limits (QSLs) define the fastest possible evolution between distinguishable quantum states, critical for quantum computing and information processing. Closed-system QSLs, such as the ML [arXiv:quant-ph/9804014] and MT [DOI:10.1103/PhysRev.41.1019] bounds, rely on energy constraints. However, open systems—subject to decoherence—require extended frameworks. Decoherence times, governed by environmental couplings, may impose additional QSLs, yet their interplay with ML/MT bounds remains unexplored. Spin chains, realizable in trapped ions [DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1394-6] and superconducting circuits, offer a many-body testbed for studying these effects. Introduction Quantum speed limits (QSLs) define the fastest possible evolution between distinguishable quantum states, critical for quantum computing and information processing. Closed-system QSLs, such as the ML [arXiv:quant-ph/9804014] and MT [DOI:10.1103/PhysRev.41.1019] bounds, rely on energy constraints. title: Non-linear Probability Model-Driven Natural Language Processing Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel non-linear probability model-driven natural language processing (NLP) algorithm designed to automatically adjust model parameters based on textual dynamism, thereby enhancing the accuracy of NLP systems. The core mechanism centers around the integration of a non-linear probabilistic model, allowing the system to adapt to evolving text patterns. Existing NLP approaches are largely static, failing to adequately address the inherent variability of natural language. This algorithm offers a significant improvement in accuracy and robustness by dynamically adjusting model parameters in response to text changes, leading to more accurate and reliable NLP results. This work addresses a critical challenge in NLP – the need for adaptive models – and presents a framework for automated parameter adjustment, paving the way for more sophisticated and versatile NLP applications.

abstract: Quantum algorithm optimization is a crucial area of research, aiming to improve the performance of quantum algorithms through intelligent parameter adjustments. This paper introduces a novel framework for adaptive quantum algorithm optimization based on quantum topology. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting quantum algorithm parameters to enhance efficiency and accuracy. We present a theoretical analysis demonstrating the effectiveness of this approach in optimizing a specific quantum algorithm, highlighting its advantages over traditional optimization techniques. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Bayesian Inference based on Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum computing to accelerate Bayesian inference. Traditional Bayesian inference suffers from significant computational bottlenecks, particularly in complex models with large datasets. We propose a novel approach leveraging the inherent parallelism of quantum computers to drastically reduce the time required for inference. Specifically, we design a quantum algorithm based on a parameterized quantum circuit (PQC) to perform Bayesian updating. This approach utilizes quantum superposition and interference to perform computations on multiple possibilities simultaneously. The core claim is that this method can significantly speed up Bayesian inference. We detail the mathematical formulation of the algorithm, including the quantum circuit representation and the key operations involved. The potential of this approach to overcome the limitations of classical Bayesian inference is discussed, highlighting the transformative impact of quantum computing on probabilistic reasoning and data analysis. The efficiency gains are expected to be particularly pronounced for problems where the prior distributions and the likelihood functions are highly correlated, allowing for efficient quantum interference.

title: Adaptive Multi-Level Quantum Degradation Model
abstract: Quantum degradation processes in complex systems are increasingly recognized as multi-level phenomena, deviating from traditional single-level models. This research introduces an adaptive multi-level quantum degradation model utilizing deep neural networks to capture the intricate dynamics of quantum system decay across multiple levels. The core claim posits that quantum degradation is not a singular event but a coordinated effect of multiple levels. The proposed model dynamically adjusts its parameters based on learned features, simulating the system's evolution over various timescales. The key mechanism involves training a deep neural network to identify and characterize degradation features at each level. The model's output, represented as (Qt), reflects the quantum state at time *t*, where Qt = (q1,t, q2,t, ..., qK,t), and *K* represents the number of levels in the system. The model's adaptive nature allows it to account for the varying degrees of degradation at each level, providing a more realistic and accurate representation of quantum decay compared to conventional single-level approaches. This work addresses a critical gap in current quantum degradation modeling techniques.

title: Title: Emergent Ontology Modeling with Adaptive Topology
abstract: This paper introduces an ontology-based system for modeling emergent phenomena through dynamic topology. We propose a novel approach that constructs a 'map' of interconnected concepts, dynamically adjusting the network topology to facilitate the emergence of novel relationships and concepts. The system utilizes a topological network to represent relationships, enabling the system to explore and generate new concepts based on the existing connections. This contrasts with static ontology systems, which lack the capacity to generate new concepts organically. The core mechanism focuses on creating a 'map' – a network representation – that allows for the self-organization of concepts through connectivity. We present a preliminary implementation illustrating the system's capabilities through a simplified example, demonstrating the system's ability to generate new concepts based on initial connections.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architectures for Quantum Computing Hardware
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum computing hardware that diverges from the traditional Von Neumann architecture. The core argument centers around leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition for inherent parallel computation, addressing limitations inherent in the conventional model. We introduce a heterogeneous quantum computing architecture built upon quantum bits (qubits) and quantum circuits, designed to facilitate data processing and control through orchestrated quantum operations. The fundamental innovation lies in moving away from the sequential processing paradigm dictated by Von Neumann architecture, offering a potentially more efficient hardware platform for quantum computations. This architecture aims to unlock significant computational speedups by exploiting the quantum mechanical properties of superposition and entanglement, moving beyond the constraints of classical bit manipulation. The design incorporates a novel control system and qubit connectivity model to maximize computational parallelism. This research contributes to the exploration of alternative hardware designs critical for the advancement of scalable and performant quantum computing systems.

title: Title: Holistic Information Encryption (HIE)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of Holistic Information Encryption (HIE), a novel cryptographic system predicated on the assumption that information possesses inherent structure. Traditional cryptographic methods often rely on complex mathematical algorithms, but HIE seeks to exploit this structure for enhanced security. The core of HIE lies in the implementation of a 'Dynamic Graph Embedding' technique, which constructs a dynamic representation of the information's structure, rendering it significantly more resistant to reverse engineering. The paper will detail the design and implementation of this algorithm, discussing its potential benefits and limitations, and ultimately, will present a preliminary assessment of its security properties. The paper will conclude with a discussion of future research directions, including exploring the scalability and application of this technique to different types of information.

title: Information-Theoretic Validation of Neural Network Representations
abstract: Evaluating the quality of learned representations within neural networks remains a significant challenge. Traditional methods often rely on task-specific performance, which can be misleading and doesn't directly address the fundamental question of how well a representation captures underlying structure in the data. This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network representation validation based on information theory. We introduce a framework utilizing concepts like mutual information and transfer entropy to quantify the predictive power and representational capacity of features extracted by a neural network. These metrics provide a statistically grounded method for comparing different architectures and understanding the information content they encode. The core claim is that current methods lack a rigorous information-theoretic foundation. This work contributes a new, objective metric for assessing neural network representations, moving beyond subjective evaluations and offering concrete statistical insights.

title: Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper introduces a novel architecture for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) designed to effectively handle multi-scale spatio-temporal data. The core concept revolves around decomposing time-series data into multiple scales, each represented by a corresponding graph structure. A GNN is then employed to learn dependencies within these individual scales, and finally, these graph representations are fused to achieve comprehensive modeling of complex spatio-temporal phenomena. The proposed approach addresses the limitations of traditional GNNs when dealing with large-scale, multi-scale data, offering improved capabilities for capturing intricate relationships. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through a theoretical analysis, highlighting its advantages over existing methods. The key innovation lies in the hierarchical graph representation and the subsequent integrated learning process, leading to enhanced performance in capturing temporal dynamics and spatial correlations. This work provides a foundational framework for advanced spatio-temporal modeling applications.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a peculiar quantum phenomenon, offers the potential for fundamentally new computational paradigms. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to optimize linear equation solving, aiming to achieve significantly enhanced efficiency and accuracy. We propose a novel optimization algorithm leveraging entangled qubit states to accelerate the solution of linear systems, demonstrating a robust and verifiable approach. The core mechanism centers around manipulating entangled states to achieve a faster convergence towards the optimal solution, while simultaneously guaranteeing the correctness of the results. This work represents a significant step toward utilizing quantum mechanics to improve computational performance.

title: Dynamic Semantic Topological Learning Network (DSTLN)
abstract: This paper introduces the Dynamic Semantic Topological Learning Network (DSTLN), a novel deep learning architecture designed to automatically learn and adapt network semantic structures by mimicking the dynamic connectivity and plasticity observed in biological neural networks. The core mechanism of DSTLN revolves around proxy nodes, each equipped with a semantic perception module and a connection strength regulation module. These modules, operating in conjunction with information exchange and competitive learning, enable the network to dynamically construct and evolve a topology that accurately reflects the underlying semantic relationships within the data. The semantic perception module utilizes an attention mechanism for encoding input data and identifying semantic information. Subsequently, the connection strength regulation module adjusts the connection strengths between nodes based on semantic similarity and the nodes' perception of the current network state, resulting in a dynamic topology that adapts over time. The proposed DSTLN offers a promising approach to enhance the robustness and generalization capabilities of deep learning models, particularly when dealing with complex and evolving datasets. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adaptation of the network topology, a feature previously absent in traditional deep learning architectures.

title: 基于自适应的神经网络的隐式学习优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithmic framework for machine learning model optimization, leveraging a dynamically adaptive neural network. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameters, failing to effectively adapt to complex data landscapes. Our proposed algorithm, termed "Adaptive Neural Optimization," dynamically adjusts learning rates and regularization parameters based on data feature analysis, aiming to significantly enhance model performance. We detail the core mechanism, including a feedback loop incorporating data characteristics, and discuss the theoretical implications and experimental validation of the approach. This work contributes to the development of more robust and adaptable machine learning models.

title: Dynamic Quantum Error Correction Code Adaptive Design
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to designing quantum error correction (QEC) codes utilizing machine learning. The core concept involves constructing an optimization model for QEC codes and employing machine learning algorithms to dynamically adjust the code's parameters based on observed decoherence rates within the qubits. Traditional QEC code design relies heavily on theoretical analysis, often lacking the adaptability required for real-world quantum systems. This proposed method addresses this limitation by introducing a learning-based system capable of self-optimization, ultimately aiming to enhance error correction capabilities. The system learns from the specific characteristics of the quantum hardware and can adapt to changing conditions, a critical step towards practical quantum computation. The primary goal is to create a system that automatically adjusts its parameters to maximize error correction performance, paving the way for more robust and reliable quantum computations. The system's efficacy is dependent on accurate measurement of decoherence and the effectiveness of the chosen machine learning algorithm.

title: Seconde révolution quantique et chimie : Un ordinateur quantique pour quoi faire ?
abstract: La chimie est souvent considérée comme l’une des applications les plus prometteuses du calcul quantique. Cette association repose sur une affinité profonde entre les lois qui gouvernent les systèmes moléculaires et les principes de l’information quantique. Pourtant, derrière cette intuition séduisante se cache une réalité scientifique et industrielle bien plus complexe. Dans cet article, nous explorons les fondements de cette promesse, ainsi que les défis algorithmiques et industriels qui conditionnent encore sa concrétisation.

title: A transformer-based multi-modal fusion framework for laryngeal lesion classification using contact endoscopy
abstract: Purpose This study introduces a novel multi-modal transformer-based framework that integrates clinical data, radiomic features, and deep learning representations for automated classification of laryngeal lesions from contact endoscopy images. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 300 patients with laryngeal lesions from three independent medical centers (Centers A, B, and C), acquiring 7,847 contact endoscopy images with narrow band imaging. Clinical variables (18 features), radiomic features extracted using PyRadiomics (156 features), and deep learning representations from three state-of-the-art architectures, ConvNeXt V2, Swin Transformer V2, and EfficientNet V2 (3,328 combined features), were systematically integrated through a six-layer transformer encoder with multi-head cross-attention mechanisms. We evaluated three feature selection strategies (LASSO, mutual information, ReliefF) and three advanced classification architectures (Vision Transformer, Attention-MLP, Graph Neural Network). The framework was developed using data from Centers A and B ( n = 230 patients) with rigorous five-fold cross-validation, and validated on an independent external test set from Center C ( n = 70 patients). Results The optimal configuration (LASSO feature selection with Vision Transformer classifier) achieved accuracy of 96.1 ± 1.0% (AUC-ROC: 0.992 ± 0.007) on training, 93.8 ± 1.4% (AUC-ROC: 0.981 ± 0.012) on internal validation, and 91.4 ± 2.1% (AUC-ROC: 0.967 ± 0.019) on external testing, with sensitivity of 90.0 ± 2.8% and specificity of 92.5 ± 2.5% on the external cohort. evidence.title: A transformer-based multi-modal fusion framework for laryngeal lesion classification using contact endoscopy
evidence.abstract: Purpose This study introduces a novel multi-modal transformer-based framework that integrates clinical data, radiomic features, and deep learning representations for automated classification of laryngeal lesions from contact endoscopy images. Methods We retrospectively enrolled 300 patients with laryngeal lesions from three independent medical centers (Centers A, B, and C), acquiring 7,847 contact endoscopy images with narrow band imaging. title: "FedWave: Code and Evaluation Logs for Stealthy Wavelet-Domain Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning"
abstract: "This dataset contains the source code and evaluation logs supporting the manuscript \"FedWave: Stealthy Wavelet-Domain Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning,\" submitted to the IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security.FedWave is an anchor-aligned wavelet-subband backdoor framework for federated learning (FL). It combines three mechanisms: (i) frequency-domain trigger embedding in the LH\/HL\/HH subbands of a one-level 2D Haar DWT, restricted to the blue channel for visual stealth; (ii) subband-wise trigger decomposition with probabilistic cross-client association, governed by an association probability p; and (iii) Anchor-Based Projection (ABP), which aligns each poisoned update to a safety band centred on a locally simulated, same-round benign update norm.The release includes the FedWave implementation, the baseline attack implementations used for comparison (BadNets, DBA, FIBA-FL, Neurotoxin), the evaluation harness for the nine defenses studied in the manuscript, and the per-round metric logs from which every table and figure is produced. All experiments use ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and GTSRB and a lightweight SimpleCNN on EMNIST, under Dirichlet non-IID client partitioning.The input datasets (CIFAR-10, GTSRB, EMNIST) are third-party public resources and are NOT redistributed here; links to their official sources are provided under Links. These artifacts are released to support reproducibility and follow-on defense research. See README for responsible-use terms. "

title: Algebraic Operator Decomposition: A Partitioned Architecture for Noise-Resilient Quantum Computing
abstract: We present an operator-decomposition architecture that mathematically maps a global operator into independently executable local operators, reducing the maximum quantum circuit depth at the cost of classical reconstruction and sampling overhead. By framing complex Quantum Circuits around an operator in a vector space that can be algebraically pre-decomposed, AOD complements quantum error correction and error-mitigation approaches by performing algebraic decomposition before quantum execution. Our approach leans in the computer science definition of a Monoid: a design pattern and mathematical concept consisting of a data type, a combining function that is associative, and a safe identity (neutral) element that does not change other values when combined. Simulation wise we define a MapReduce programming model where the addition (+) is the reducer, thus leveraging a naturally stable commutative monoid which carries zero "negative-probability tax" or phase conflicts. Furthermore, we define a Vector Space of Linear Operators over Additive Abelian Groups that benefit from this paradigm, including: Inner Products, Series expansions, Traces and Convolutions. Finally, we present the mathematical foundations and simulation results for this paradigm.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Neural Network Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive neural network optimization algorithm designed to enhance model generalization by dynamically adjusting network parameters based on training data. Traditional neural network optimization methods often rely on static learning rates, which can lead to suboptimal performance when data shifts significantly. Our proposed algorithm incorporates a "dynamic learning rate" mechanism, allowing the network to adapt its learning rate during training to effectively navigate the data landscape and prevent local optima. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop based on data distribution to dynamically adjust parameters, resulting in improved generalization capabilities. We present a comprehensive analysis and evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

title: Title: Quantum Error Mitigation via Adaptive Probabilistic Noise
abstract: Quantum error mitigation (QEM) is a crucial technique for enhancing the reliability of quantum computations. Current methods, however, often rely on fixed noise levels, which can be computationally demanding and limit efficiency. This paper introduces a novel QEM algorithm utilizing a Bayesian neural network to dynamically adjust the probabilistic noise applied during error correction. Our design systematically learns the optimal noise level for each quantum state, continuously adapting to the evolving error profile. This adaptive approach promises to significantly improve both error suppression and computational efficiency compared to existing methods. The proposed algorithm offers a fundamentally new way to optimize error mitigation, paving the way for more robust and practical quantum computations.

title: Adaptive Neural Networks with Variable Parameters
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to neural network design – Adaptive Neural Networks with Variable Parameters (ANVPs). The core idea is to move away from the traditional fixed-parameter paradigm and embrace dynamic adaptation. Instead of fixed weights and biases, ANVPs incorporate variable parameter modules whose parameters are adjusted iteratively based on input data and error feedback. This allows the network to dynamically modify its structure and connection strengths, potentially leading to more efficient learning and improved performance across a wider range of tasks. We explore the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlining the core mechanisms and highlighting how it differs from existing neural network architectures. The paper focuses on the fundamental design and principles, without detailing any specific experimental implementations. The goal is to provide a conceptual framework for future research in this area. ---

title: Predictive Coding with Latent Temporal Dynamics
abstract: Standard predictive coding (PC) models often struggle to represent and predict temporal sequences effectively. These models typically operate on static predictions, failing to account for the inherent dynamic evolution of underlying temporal patterns. This paper proposes an extension to PC that addresses this limitation by integrating a learned latent temporal dynamical system. This system models the evolution of the predicted signal itself, providing the model with the ability to anticipate future states based on past temporal patterns. The core innovation lies in dynamically predicting the prediction, creating a recursive and adaptive framework. The model's performance is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual demonstrations, highlighting its improved capacity for capturing and predicting complex temporal dynamics compared to traditional PC approaches. We demonstrate that the inclusion of this latent temporal dynamics significantly enhances the model's ability to represent and predict temporal data, offering a more robust and nuanced approach to predictive coding.

title: ##基于多模态协同推理的知识图谱增强
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to enhancing knowledge graphs (KGs) by leveraging multimodal collaborative reasoning. Traditional KGs primarily rely on textual information, often lacking the richness and contextual understanding provided by other modalities like images and audio. Our proposed method addresses this limitation by integrating diverse data sources—text, images, and audio—through a collaborative reasoning framework. We introduce a multimodal fusion model that maps each modality into a unified vector space, enabling effective integration of knowledge. Subsequently, we employ graph neural networks (GNNs) to perform multi-modal knowledge fusion and reasoning, dynamically enriching the KG's semantic representation and enhancing its inference capabilities. The core claim of this work is that dynamic KG enhancement can be achieved through multimodal data collaboration. The core mechanism involves multimodal fusion and GNN-based reasoning. This research represents a significant step beyond traditional single-modality KGs, offering a more comprehensive and robust knowledge representation system. ---

title: Probabilistic Programming for Explainable AI – Causal Bayesian Networks
abstract: The increasing deployment of complex AI models, particularly deep neural networks, raises significant concerns about their interpretability and trustworthiness. Existing XAI techniques often provide post-hoc explanations that lack a clear connection to the model's underlying reasoning. This paper proposes a novel approach to building truly explainable AI systems by leveraging probabilistic programming languages and causal Bayesian networks. The core idea is to explicitly represent the model's decision-making process through a causal Bayesian network, which allows for the tracing of influence and identification of key features. We demonstrate how probabilistic programming facilitates the construction of these networks, providing a framework for generating transparent and understandable AI systems. The proposed method shifts the focus from black-box model explanations to a white-box understanding of the model's causal structure, thereby addressing a critical limitation in current XAI methodologies. This approach offers a robust foundation for building AI systems that not only achieve high accuracy but also provide clear and justifiable explanations for their decisions.

title: Dimension Generalization and Quantum Entanglement Resonance
abstract: This paper investigates the interplay between dimension generalization and quantum entanglement resonance, proposing a novel framework for simulating high-dimensional spatial geometry using quantum entanglement. We explore a "dimension re-shape" algorithm, leveraging instantaneous correlations within entangled states, to predict the limits of quantum computation. The core mechanism centers on inducing resonant behavior within the quantum simulator, ultimately revealing potential bottlenecks and limitations associated with current computational paradigms. The study aims to provide a theoretical foundation for understanding and potentially expanding the capabilities of quantum computing.

title: A Continual Learning Framework Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel continual learning framework inspired by the mechanisms observed in biological neural networks. Traditional continual learning approaches often suffer from catastrophic forgetting and limited adaptability. This framework addresses these challenges by integrating key biological learning principles, including memory replay, sparse coding, and experience replay. We aim to create a more robust and efficient system capable of learning continuously across diverse and changing environments. The core claim of this work is that mimicking the dynamic learning capabilities of biological neural networks can lead to a superior continual learning framework. We detail the underlying mechanisms and theoretical foundations of the framework, emphasizing the use of memory replay to mitigate forgetting, sparse coding to improve representation efficiency, and experience replay to facilitate efficient learning from past experiences. We present a detailed formulation of the framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. This research contributes to the advancement of continual learning by providing a biologically-inspired approach that potentially overcomes the limitations of existing methods. ---

title: Multi-Modal Knowledge Graph Reasoning with Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper investigates the challenges and proposes a novel approach to multi-modal knowledge graph reasoning by incorporating causal discovery mechanisms. Traditional knowledge graph reasoning often relies solely on correlation analysis, which can lead to inaccurate and misleading inferences. We argue that explicitly modeling causal relationships within knowledge graphs significantly improves the robustness and explainability of reasoning processes. Our method leverages causal inference algorithms to identify and utilize causal links within the graph, guiding the reasoning process with a more reliable understanding of the underlying mechanisms. We present a framework that integrates multi-modal data (text, structured data, and potentially images) and applies causal discovery to uncover the true causal relationships, leading to more accurate and interpretable reasoning outcomes. The core claim is that the introduction of causal discovery enhances both the accuracy and interpretability of multi-modal knowledge graph reasoning. The proposed mechanism utilizes causal inference algorithms to identify and utilize these relationships, and this represents a novel approach compared to existing correlation-based methods. This research addresses the limitations of current approaches by prioritizing causal understanding over simple association.

title: Dynamic Topology Generation for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of quantum computing, safeguarding the integrity of quantum information. Current error correction schemes rely on static topologies, which can be inefficient and limit scalability. This paper proposes a dynamic topology generation technique, utilizing the inherent structure of quantum systems to dynamically optimize qubit layouts, thereby significantly enhancing the resilience of quantum error correction protocols. The core mechanism centers around an automated optimization algorithm that intelligently adjusts qubit arrangements to minimize error propagation. This innovation offers a fundamentally new approach to quantum error correction, potentially leading to more robust and scalable quantum computing platforms. The proposed method is designed to enhance error correction capabilities, offering a pathway towards practical quantum information processing.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Global Horizontal Irradiance Estimation in an Arid Coastal Climate
abstract: Accurate estimation of global horizontal irradiance (GHI) is relevant for characterizing solar resources in regions with limited measurement infrastructure. This study compared six machine learning models Polynomial Ridge Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, Artificial Neural Network, and K–Nearest Neighbors for the contemporaneous estimation of GHI at a five-minute resolution in an arid coastal climate. After quality control and restriction to daytime periods, 45,024 observations were analyzed using five external chronological blocks with an expanding-window scheme, generating 31,517 out-of-sample estimates. XGBoost achieved the highest R2(0.657±0.192) and the lowest RMSE (108.01 ± 13.67 W m−2), whereas Random Forest yielded lower MAE, WMAPE, and MASE values. DM–HAC sensitivity analysis favored XGBoost under squared-error loss for six of the seven evaluated bandwidths, whereas no significant difference between XGBoost and Random Forest was found under absolute-error loss. None of the models achieved the nominal conformal coverage level of 90%; XGBoost showed the highest empirical coverage and the narrowest prediction intervals (PICP = 0.791; PINAW = 0.312). Predictor-set reduction improved the performance of four of the six algorithms. Overall, XGBoost and Random Forest exhibited complementary performance profiles, indicating that model selection should jointly consider predictive accuracy, temporal stability, predictor sensitivity, and uncertainty.

title: Basic Concepts and Techniques in Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This chapter lays the essential groundwork for understanding sentiment analysis. It begins by defining sentiment and its various classification types, including basic polarity (positive, negative, and neutral), fine-grained emotions based on Ekman's and Plutchik's models, and aspect-based sentiment analysis. The chapter then explores major data sources such as social media platforms, customer reviews, news articles, forums, blogs, and customer service interactions. Core techniques are systematically introduced, covering lexical-based approaches, traditional machine learning methods, and deep learning architectures. Special attention is given to non-textual modalities, including speech sentiment analysis through acoustic features and visual sentiment analysis via facial expressions and body language. The chapter concludes with practical guidance on evaluation metrics and the considerations for selecting appropriate techniques based on task requirements, data characteristics, and computational resources.

title: Multi-Harness Reinforcement Learning for Coding Agents: Training Gains and Harness Dependence
abstract: Recent systems train coding agents with reinforcement learning (RL) on trajectories collected through multiple execution harnesses. However, gains under the training harnesses leave open whether the improvements transfer to unseen interfaces and how they depend on reward normalization. We present a controlled study that measures RL gains under fixed harnesses and compares the same models across harnesses. We train two Qwen3-8B RL variants from the same supervised fine-tuning (SFT) checkpoint using identical replay data. They differ only in whether rewards for each task are normalized within each harness (Within) or across harnesses (Cross). On SWE-bench Verified, we identify three main findings: (i) Multi-harness RL yields modest gains over the SFT baseline under both normalization rules. Across the four training harnesses, the estimated mean improvements are +0.48 and +0.77 percentage points for Within and Cross, respectively. (ii) Cross increases the fraction of trajectories with nonzero advantage but provides no consistent advantage over Within on an unseen harness across training seeds and evaluation budgets; neither rule significantly improves over SFT on this harness. (iii) Performance varies substantially more across harnesses than with RL training. After averaging over model variants, the highest and lowest source-harness solve rates differ by 7.13 percentage points, far exceeding the estimated training gains. Even after multi-harness RL, the observed performance differences across execution interfaces remain substantially larger than either the gains from training or the differences between normalization rules.

title: Para-Pipe: Exploiting Hierarchical Operator Parallelism of ML Computational Graphs on SoCs
abstract: As edge-based deep learning applications become more complex, optimizing performance on heterogeneous System-on-Chips (SoCs) presents unique challenges. Traditional pipelining techniques distributing the computation across different on-chip processing units, while effective for throughput, do not address the latency demands posed by modern neural networks with complex interdependencies and extensive operator parallelism. There is a potential in leveraging operator parallelism to enable concurrent execution across multiple processing units, thereby reducing inference latency. However, prioritizing pipelining or parallel execution often necessitates a compromise, where optimizing one performance metric adversely impacts the other. This paper introduces Para-Pipe, a hierarchical mapping framework that integrates intra- and inter-stage operator parallelism within a pipelined architecture. Para-Pipe navigates the trade-off between throughput and latency by selectively fine-tuning parallelism levels within and across pipeline stages. This strategy can significantly reduce inter-processor communication overhead, significantly improving energy efficiency. Our evaluation demonstrates that Para-Pipe generates multiple Pareto-optimal configurations, achieving a balance between throughput and latency on an Amlogic SoC equipped with ARM big.LITTLE CPUs and GPU, as well as the Black Sesame Technology SoC featuring a deep learning accelerator and two DSPs. More importantly, throughput-optimized configurations under Para-Pipe on Amlogic SoC show an average energy efficiency improvement of 11.0% over purely pipelined strategies and 23.3% relative to non-pipelined parallel execution.

title: Geometric Ceilings on Time-Frequency Masking for Single-Channel Separation
abstract: Most single-channel separators estimate a source by applying a real gain to the mixture in each time-frequency bin. The optimum of that format, which the oracle masks used as bounds do not attain, is the orthogonal projection of the source onto the line spanned by the mixture, its residual set by the angle between them. Locating an estimator reduces to the block structure of a real-linear operator on stacked spectra, giving a chain of four nested classes whose three larger terms match three assumptions on the prior: zero means, circularity and absence of inter-frequency coupling. Held fixed the chain is a cascade of four orthogonal projections; refitted per frame it collapses onto its first term, attributing the whole residual to one missing real parameter per bin, the phase. When the phase posterior is symmetric about the mixture direction, the minimum mean-square estimate falls back onto the line, with gain the posterior mean of the oracle gain and excess error its variance. On MUSDB18 a posterior mean under a non-circular Gaussian-mixture prior leaves the class yet stays 11.44 dB under the per-frame ceiling, which four times as many components and 7.5x the data do not close; a closed-form gate attributes some 70% of it, in decibels, to the predicted variance. The widest fixed class stays 6.70 dB under the same ceiling. Leaving the class and minimising squared error are conflicting requests: the barrier lies in the criterion rather than in the prior.

title: Affective publics in Arabic YouTube
abstract: What is the emotional register of Arabic YouTube's affective publics? To investigate this, we analyzed 67,725 YouTube comments collected around socio-political topics associated with Yemen, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Jordan, and Syria using a unified sentiment-and-emotion pipeline. Our results profile a single regional affective public rather than five separate national ones. Sentiment is overwhelmingly negative across all five country-oriented corpora, and the country-level emotion profiles are structurally similar. This shared register still accommodates some regional variations: discourse is organized around country-level political actors and cross-border historical trauma figures, and grief singularizes Iraq from the other countries. The differences in emotional register also tracks lived political causes rather than fixed categories, which we observe from patterns of the valence of US-related content, that tracks the presence or absence of direct US military engagement. Our work shows that the emotional register of Arabic YouTube's affective publics is a shared one that is historically layered and geographically conditioned, which has implications for public diplomacy in the MENA region.

title: 基于多模态数据融合的知识图谱构建
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for knowledge graph construction leveraging multi-modal data fusion. Recognizing the limitations of traditional approaches that rely on single data type, we propose a method designed to integrate and enrich knowledge representations through the synergistic combination of diverse data modalities. The core of this framework involves a sophisticated data fusion mechanism that intelligently combines and contextualizes information extracted from textual, visual, and sensor data. This integration enables the construction of knowledge graphs with enhanced representational capacity and adaptability to evolving real-world scenarios. The proposed approach addresses the challenge of heterogeneous data and offers a pathway towards more robust and nuanced knowledge representation. The resulting knowledge graph will provide a foundation for advanced applications in areas such as semantic search, anomaly detection, and intelligent decision-making.

title: Quantum Algorithm Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum Algorithm Parameter Adjustment (QAPA) presents a novel approach to quantum algorithm optimization by dynamically adjusting parameters during the execution of a quantum computation. This paper details the design and implementation of QAPA, highlighting its mechanism of leveraging quantum properties to achieve increased efficiency. We explore the core concepts and mathematical foundations underpinning this technique, demonstrating its potential to surpass traditional parameter tuning methods. This work contributes to the field of quantum algorithm design by providing a robust and automated framework for optimization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Geometry Simulation
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new perspective on geometric simulations, promising enhanced precision and the ability to model complex phenomena previously inaccessible to classical approaches. This paper explores a novel framework for geometric simulation leveraging quantum entanglement, focusing on the potential to accurately represent and predict geometric properties through the subtle influence of entangled states. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts geometric transformations based on entangled correlations, aiming to bridge the gap between classical geometry and quantum mechanics. This research addresses the limitations of traditional methods by incorporating a non-linear geometric process driven by quantum entanglement. The core claim is that this framework provides a pathway towards more accurate geometric predictions and allows for a deeper understanding of geometric transformations.

title: Title: Geometric Topology for Algorithmic Diversity in Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum machine learning holds immense potential for revolutionizing various fields, but its inherent complexity necessitates innovative approaches to algorithm design. Geometric topology, a field that studies the properties of spaces defined by continuous functions, offers a promising avenue for addressing this challenge. This paper proposes a novel geometric topology framework for quantum machine learning, aiming to generate diverse and robust algorithms by systematically exploring different geometric structures representing the data and the machine learning algorithm. We outline a method for generating and manipulating geometric shapes, emphasizing their role as fundamental building blocks for diverse and stable quantum machine learning models. The core mechanism centers on leveraging the inherent properties of geometric shapes to create a dynamic landscape of possibilities, thereby promoting algorithmic diversity. This research explores the potential of using geometric topology to overcome limitations of current quantum machine learning techniques and advance the field.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Quantum Circuit Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for solving complex problems intractable for classical computers. However, the inherent complexity of quantum circuits necessitates sophisticated optimization techniques. This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive quantum circuit optimization algorithm, designed to automatically adjust quantum gate parameters based on the circuit's dynamic state. The algorithm leverages a feedback loop that continuously monitors the circuit's evolution, dynamically re-optimizing gate parameters to minimize error rates and maximize performance. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and demonstrate its effectiveness through a series of rigorous simulations and experiments. The core mechanism focuses on a closed-loop optimization process that adapts to the circuit's inherent variability. The results indicate a significant improvement in quantum circuit performance compared to existing static optimization methods. We conclude by discussing potential applications and future research directions.

title: Title: Self-Organizing Quantum Landscapes for Algorithm Design
abstract: Quantum algorithms are increasingly vital for tackling complex problems in diverse fields, from drug discovery to materials science. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems often necessitates specialized algorithms tailored to specific scenarios. This paper explores the potential of utilizing self-organizing quantum landscapes – dynamic, evolving environments designed to guide the formation of intricate quantum states – to facilitate novel algorithm design. This approach promises a more flexible and adaptable framework compared to traditional algorithmic methods. We propose a novel method leveraging a 'quantum gradient' to sculpt the landscape, encouraging the emergence of complex, multi-scale quantum configurations, which we believe will be crucial for discovering new algorithmic solutions. This work builds upon existing research in quantum control and landscape design, presenting a fundamentally new approach with the potential to significantly broaden the scope of quantum algorithm development.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive graph neural network (DAGNN) architecture designed to optimize network performance through automated structural adjustments. Traditional graph neural networks often rely on fixed, pre-defined structures, limiting their adaptability to diverse data. Our approach leverages a dynamic self-adaptation algorithm that continuously refines the network's topology based on input characteristics, thereby enhancing predictive accuracy and generalization capabilities. We present a comprehensive evaluation demonstrating the effectiveness of this method compared to existing DAGNNs.

title: Probability and Formal Verification: A Combined Approach
abstract: Probability and formal verification are two distinct yet complementary approaches to mathematical validation. This paper explores the synergy between these techniques, proposing a novel framework leveraging probability reasoning to rigorously validate mathematical theorems and proofs. The core claim centers on the development of a probabilistic verification system that enhances the reliability and reproducibility of mathematical investigations. Traditional methods often rely on manual analysis, while this work introduces a more automated and robust approach facilitated by the integration of probabilistic inference and formal verification. This research aims to provide a more effective and dependable method for validating mathematical concepts, ultimately contributing to the advancement of mathematical knowledge.

title: Data Compression based on Topology
abstract: This paper proposes a novel data compression technique leveraging the inherent topology of data streams. Traditional data compression methods often rely on statistical analysis of data patterns, which can be inefficient for complex data flows exhibiting significant topological relationships. Our approach, termed "Topology-based Data Compression" (TDC), represents data as a topological graph, exploiting the compression potential within these structures. The core mechanism involves mapping data elements to nodes in a graph and edges representing relationships between them. This graph is then compressed using standard graph compression algorithms. We demonstrate the potential of TDC to achieve higher compression ratios, particularly for data streams with strong topological correlations, compared to traditional methods. The key innovation lies in recognizing and utilizing the topological structure as a fundamental component of the compression process, moving beyond purely statistical analysis. We present a theoretical framework and outline the core elements of the TDC methodology, highlighting its advantages and potential applications.

Traditional approaches often struggle to accurately model complex phenomena, and this algorithm aims to overcome this limitation through a unique approach that correlates resonance frequencies across multiple scales. The core mechanism centers on establishing a quantum entanglement network to capture and interpret subtle shifts in resonant frequencies, ultimately enabling prediction of emergent behavior. The algorithm's potential impact lies in advancing our understanding of systems exhibiting complex dynamics and identifying critical thresholds influencing behavior.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的程序合成 (Self-Adaptive Neural Network Program Synthesis - SANNPS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis leveraging self-adaptive neural networks. The Self-Adaptive Neural Network Program Synthesis (SANNPS) system automatically generates code from high-level specifications, addressing the significant challenges associated with traditional program synthesis methods. The core mechanism involves a neural network architecture designed for continuous adaptation based on the feedback from the generated code's execution. The system iteratively refines its code generation process, improving both accuracy and efficiency. This approach promises to dramatically enhance programming productivity and potentially democratize software development by reducing reliance on manual coding expertise. The primary contributions of this work are the architecture design of the adaptive neural network, the feedback mechanism for continuous learning, and the overall framework for automated program synthesis. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this methodology through a series of illustrative examples.

title: Graph-Based Evolutionary Algorithms for Software Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of evolutionary algorithms to the problem of software design, specifically focusing on graph-based representations of software systems. The core argument is that evolutionary algorithms can achieve superior performance when applied directly to graph-structured problems, leading to more effective exploration of design spaces compared to traditional methods. We introduce a novel evolutionary algorithm designed to operate directly on a graph, allowing for the efficient generation and evaluation of architectural designs. The algorithm employs a genetic operator framework adapted for graph manipulation, including mutation and crossover operations that preserve graph structure and connectivity. The key innovation lies in the direct manipulation of the graph representation, enabling the algorithm to directly optimize design attributes such as modularity, cohesion, and coupling. The results, although not presented through experimental data due to the focus on the algorithmic design, demonstrate the potential of this approach for tackling complex software design challenges. We outline the algorithm's components, detailing the representation of software systems as graphs, the genetic operators used, and the fitness function employed for evaluating designs. The presented framework provides a foundation for future research in applying evolutionary algorithms to a broader range of software design problems.

title: Non-Spin State Quantum Computation: A Benchmarking Experimental Scheme
abstract: This paper presents a novel experimental scheme for quantum computation utilizing non-spin states, specifically electronic orbital states, as quantum bits (qubits). The core claim is that leveraging non-spin states offers a pathway to simplify qubit fabrication and manipulation, ultimately enhancing the scalability of quantum computing. This scheme focuses on establishing a benchmarking experimental framework to validate the computational capabilities of such a system. The proposed methodology avoids the complexities often associated with controlling and maintaining the delicate quantum states of spins. Instead, it proposes utilizing precisely controlled electronic orbital states, offering a potentially more manageable system for early-stage quantum computation. The presented framework includes a detailed description of the experimental setup, the quantum gates being implemented, and the methods for verifying the computational outcomes. The potential impact of this approach on the future of quantum computing is discussed, emphasizing the shift towards more accessible and scalable quantum technologies.

title: 基于量子拓扑的几何变换算法的优化
abstract: Quantum topology offers a fundamentally new approach to geometric optimization, leveraging the unique properties of quantum systems to achieve automated, efficient solutions. This paper explores the application of quantum topology to a specific geometric transformation problem, presenting a novel algorithm that circumvents the limitations of traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism centers around the design of a quantum-inspired transformation process, designed to exploit quantum entanglement and superposition to guide the optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a detailed analysis of a chosen geometric transformation, highlighting its advantages in terms of speed and accuracy. The research investigates the potential for future expansion and refinement of this quantum-based optimization technique, providing a foundation for further exploration into this promising field.

abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to enable adaptive geometric transformation and optimization within a system. We introduce a novel mechanism leveraging quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust the geometry of a system, offering a potentially transformative approach to geometric manipulation and optimization. The core claim is that a system capable of exploiting quantum entanglement can achieve more effective geometric transformations and optimization compared to conventional methods. This work explores the principles of entanglement-based geometry and proposes a framework for utilizing this phenomenon to guide the evolution of complex systems. The theoretical foundation rests on a simplified model of geometric transformations and explores the implications of quantum entanglement on these transformations. This research addresses a long-standing challenge in computational geometry, potentially opening avenues for advanced optimization and control within various fields.

title: Dynamic Circuit Synthesis via Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to digital circuit synthesis leveraging the power of Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning (ERL). Traditional circuit synthesis methods often rely on deterministic algorithms that struggle to effectively manage the complexity and dynamism inherent in modern design requirements. This research addresses this limitation by implementing an ERL system capable of iteratively generating and refining circuit designs. The core of the system involves an evolutionary algorithm that explores the design space, guided by a reinforcement learning agent that dynamically learns a reward function based on design rules and constraints. This dynamic reward function enables the system to adapt to evolving design priorities and optimize for performance metrics such as delay, power consumption, and area. The resulting system demonstrates the potential to overcome the drawbacks of conventional synthesis techniques, offering a more robust and adaptive solution for complex circuit design problems. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of evolutionary search and reinforcement learning, creating a system that can autonomously learn and refine circuit designs within highly constrained and dynamic environments. The system is designed for adaptability and efficiency, and the potential for its application in various digital design domains is significant.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Probability Geometry Topology Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize probabilistic geometry analysis, specifically focusing on the topology of complex structures. We propose a novel tool, a quantum-enhanced probability geometry framework, that utilizes entanglement to dramatically improve pattern recognition and structure assessment of topological phenomena. The core claim is that entanglement can unlock previously inaccessible insights into the inherent structure of topological spaces, offering a significant advancement over current analytical methods. We detail the mechanism behind this approach, outlining the quantum entanglement process and its implications for topological analysis. The paper presents a preliminary framework and discusses potential future research directions.

title: The Impact of Adaptive Graphs on Non-Linear Machine Learning for Environmental Change Prediction
abstract: This research investigates a novel machine learning approach leveraging adaptive graphs to predict environmental change and ecosystem evolution. Traditional machine learning often relies on static models, limiting the capacity to effectively model complex environmental dynamics. This paper introduces a new method centered around adaptive graphs, dynamically adjusting graph parameters to enhance model adaptability and precision. The core mechanism focuses on creating a system where the graph's structure evolves in response to environmental shifts, offering a more robust and nuanced prediction capability. This work addresses a critical challenge in environmental modeling, aiming to surpass the limitations of static approaches through dynamic graph manipulation. The research demonstrates the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary analysis, highlighting its potential for improved environmental forecasting.

title: Quantum Topological Optimization of Hidden Matrices
abstract: Quantum topological optimization is a rapidly growing field with the potential to revolutionize quantum computing. This paper investigates a novel approach to optimizing hidden matrix properties using a dynamically adjusted topology. We introduce a quantum topological deformation mechanism that allows the algorithm to automatically tailor the structure of hidden matrices based on the specific characteristics of the target task. This optimization aims to enhance quantum computation efficiency. The core mechanism involves leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum states to dynamically adjust the matrix's structure. The algorithm demonstrates a significant improvement in the performance of quantum computations compared to traditional approaches. This work presents a new framework for optimizing quantum matrix properties, offering a pathway towards more efficient and robust quantum algorithms.

title: Domain-Adaptive Function Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework, Domain-Adaptive Function Analysis (DAFA), for automated function generation and optimization within specific domains. Traditional function analysis methods often require manual design, while DAFA strives to provide a tool that dynamically generates and refines functions based on the characteristics of the domain. The core mechanism of DAFA leverages domain-adaptive function analysis to automatically generate suitable functions and then iteratively optimize these functions for enhanced performance within the designated domain. This approach significantly reduces the need for manual intervention, streamlining complex model analysis and simulation.

title: Biological Foundation Models for Complex Disease Research and Clinical Translation
abstract: Complex diseases, including cancer, rare genetic disorders, neurodevelopmental and psychiatric conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, arise from interactions among genetic variation, gene regulation, and cellular states that are difficult to capture using a single data type or biological scale. Biological foundation models address this challenge by treating nucleotides and genes as tokens and learning representations that can be transferred to downstream biomedical and clinical tasks. In this review, we examine two major model classes, genomic sequence foundation models and cell foundation models, and compare their tokenization strategies, model architectures, pretraining objectives, and adaptation methods. We summarize their emerging applications in regulatory variant interpretation, disease-associated cell-state analysis, drug-response prediction, and therapeutic target discovery across complex diseases. We distinguish applications supported by experimental or retrospective validation from those that remain primarily computational or conceptual. We further discuss key challenges to clinical translation, including multimodal data integration, model interpretability, benchmarking, patient-specific prediction, and privacy protection. We highlight future opportunities to integrate biological foundation models with emerging frameworks of medical digital twins, agentic AI, and federated learning. By linking model design to translational goals, this review provides a practical framework for evaluating biological foundation models and their readiness for complex disease research and clinical use.

title: Real and Synthetic Income Datasets for Comparative Statistical and Machine Learning Analysis
abstract: This dataset contains a real Adult Income dataset and an author-generated synthetic income dataset prepared for comparative statistical and machine learning analysis. The real dataset is based on the Adult dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, while the synthetic dataset was developed as a Bangladesh-oriented tabular income dataset using demographic, educational, employment, working-hour, experience, and income-related variables. The datasets are provided to support the comparison of real and synthetic tabular income data in terms of their structure, distributions, statistical relationships, and usefulness for machine learning experiments. The accompanying analysis includes data inspection, preprocessing, descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, statistical testing, classification experiments, class-imbalance handling, and model evaluation. The machine learning analysis includes Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost, with additional experiments using class weighting and Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) where applicable. Evaluation measures include accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, ROC-AUC, and Balanced Error Rate (BER). The synthetic dataset is intended as a controlled data resource for methodological comparison and experimentation. It should not be interpreted as nationally representative or as observed income data from the Bangladeshi population. In particular, the relationships within the synthetic data may reflect the assumptions and construction process used to generate the data rather than naturally occurring socioeconomic relationships. The repository is intended to support transparency, reproducibility, and future reuse of the datasets and associated analysis materials. The real and synthetic datasets should be considered separately because their variables, target representations, and data-generation processes differ.

title: Quantum Computing Basics
abstract: This chapter lays the foundation for understanding how quantum computers differ fundamentally from classical computers. It begins with the familiar territory of classical bits—binary units of zeros and ones—before moving to their quantum counterpart, the qubit. The chapter introduces the algebra of quantum mechanics—bras, kets, inner and outer products—and shows how they enable the description of quantum states and transformations. It also introduces the principles of measurement, quantum algorithms (Deutsch and Deutsch–Jozsa, Grover), and the role of unitarity in ensuring reversibility and probability conservation. Finally, the chapter broadens the horizon beyond qubits to qudits, where higher-dimensional systems promise richer computation and shorter circuits. Quantum errors are ubiquitous in all hardware due to inevitable and unwanted interaction with the environment. Amplitude damping errors occur because of energy loss, such as a photon escaping from a quantum system caused by interactions with the environment.

title: EvalMem: An Operation-Level Diagnostic Framework for Long-Term Memory Systems
abstract: Long-horizon interactions with LLM-based assistants require memory systems that preserve and update user states, preferences, and interaction histories. Existing evaluations report end-to-end QA accuracy and cannot determine whether errors arise from encoding, retrieval, or generation. We introduce EvalMem, an operation-level diagnostic framework with three parallel Examiners. For each query, the Encoding Examiner checks whether the target fact is stored, the Retrieval Examiner assesses whether the native retriever returns usable evidence, and the Generation Examiner tests whether the model can answer from oracle evidence. Their outputs form fine-grained multi-label defect codes. To improve store-level diagnosis, we adapt agentic RAG with a recall-first strategy that searches using both the query and source evidence, increasing recall of present evidence on LoCoMo from 70.2% to 95.6%. Evaluations of seven memory systems on LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S, and dynamic DynaMem-Bench identify retrieval as the most frequently attributed failure layer; in default LoCoMo, retrieval defects reach 22.1%, compared with 7.7% for encoding and 6.5% for generation. Guided by this diagnosis, MemWiki, a search-friendly auxiliary structure built from each system's memory export, improves mean accuracy by 2.5 and 2.3 percentage points on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, respectively.
