title: Title: Universal Quantum State Representation (QSR)
abstract: Quantum state representation is a cornerstone of quantum information processing, yet current methods often lack a robust, geometric framework for manipulation and analysis. This paper introduces Universal Quantum State Representation (QSR), a novel system for encoding and manipulating quantum states through a layered, dynamically evolving geometric structure. QSR leverages discrete, high-dimensional geometric transformations to provide a more intuitive and flexible approach compared to traditional methods. We demonstrate the efficacy of QSR through a series of illustrative examples, highlighting its potential to simplify complex quantum computations and facilitate deeper insights into quantum information dynamics. This work provides a foundational framework for advancing quantum state representation and enabling new algorithmic possibilities.

This work provides a foundational framework for advancing quantum state representation and enabling new algorithmic possibilities.

title: Based on Information Entropy: Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to program synthesis leveraging the concept of information entropy. The core idea is to quantify the uncertainty or exploration potential within the search space of possible program solutions. By measuring the entropy of candidate programs, we can prioritize exploration in regions with higher entropy, leading to more effective search and ultimately, the generation of higher-quality programs. Traditional program synthesis techniques often rely on heuristics or probabilistic models, which can be inefficient in exploring complex solution spaces. Our method provides a more principled approach by grounding the search process in the theoretical framework of information entropy. We propose a framework for calculating and utilizing entropy metrics within a program synthesis algorithm, offering a potentially significant improvement in synthesis efficiency and program quality. The presented approach demonstrates the potential to guide the search process towards more promising solutions, overcoming limitations of purely heuristic-based methods.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topology Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm based on the principles of nonlinear geometry topology. We propose a framework that integrates topological concepts, specifically self-intersection and self-similarity, into the optimization process. The core mechanism leverages the inherent structural properties of topological spaces to dynamically adjust optimization strategies, enabling the discovery of global optima within complex geometric spaces. The algorithm's novelty lies in its automatic adaptation of optimization parameters through the manipulation of topology, offering a potentially more efficient and robust approach compared to traditional methods. We detail the algorithm's design, its performance evaluation, and potential applications in various geometric optimization problems.

title: Probabilistic Robotics with Bayesian Filtering for Uncertain Environments
abstract: This paper presents a novel framework for probabilistic robotics leveraging Bayesian filtering to address the challenges of operating in highly uncertain environments. Traditional approaches often employ simplifying assumptions regarding noise and model inaccuracies, leading to suboptimal performance in real-world scenarios. This work introduces a refined methodology that directly incorporates both sensor noise and model uncertainties within a Bayesian filtering framework. The core of the approach lies in utilizing the Kalman filter and its extensions to recursively estimate the state of a robot while accounting for the inherent uncertainties. We detail the mathematical formulation, focusing on the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) and Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to handle non-linear systems. Furthermore, we explore methods for adaptive tuning of the filter parameters and discuss the impact of different noise models on the overall performance. The presented framework demonstrates improved robustness and accuracy compared to conventional probabilistic robotics techniques when dealing with complex, real-world environments. The system's effectiveness is primarily assessed through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, without requiring experimental validation.

title: High-Dimensional Data Space Probability Optimization
abstract: High-dimensional data analysis presents significant challenges due to the complexity of parameter adjustments. This paper proposes a novel optimization algorithm based on the probability distribution within high-dimensional data spaces. The core mechanism leverages the dynamic evolution of probability distributions to automatically adjust data distribution parameters, ultimately enhancing data analysis and modeling accuracy. This approach aims to address the inherent difficulties in parameter tuning within high-dimensional datasets. We present a framework that intelligently adapts the data distribution to optimize model performance and robustness.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture design based on graph-based models. We propose a method that automatically optimizes neural network structures by leveraging the inherent graph structure. This approach aims to enhance model generalization capabilities through intelligent adjustments to the network's connections and weights. The core of the design relies on representing the neural network as a graph, allowing for dynamic control of node and edge attributes to facilitate automated learning and refinement. title: Title: Fractal Dimension-Based Algorithmic Complexity Analysis
abstract: Fractal dimension, a measure of irregularity and complexity, offers a novel approach to quantifying algorithmic complexity. This paper presents a framework for dynamically calculating fractal dimensions for each algorithm based on its core operations, utilizing automated optimization to minimize complexity. The core mechanism involves defining fractal dimensions as inherent properties of the algorithm's structure and employing optimization to refine these dimensions, leading to a rigorous and automated method for assessing algorithm behavior and guiding design. The proposed approach represents a significant advancement over existing complexity analysis, providing a quantifiable and adaptable tool for optimizing algorithm performance.

title: Dynamic Machine Learning Adaptive Model Construction
abstract: Dynamic Machine Learning Adaptive Model Construction presents a novel framework for machine learning model creation that leverages an adaptive model adjustment mechanism to optimize the model's parameters. This approach offers improved efficiency and flexibility compared to traditional methods relying on manual parameter adjustments. The core concept centers around a dynamically adjusted model state, allowing the model to continuously refine its parameters based on feedback and data, ultimately leading to enhanced performance. This research focuses on establishing a robust and efficient methodology for building adaptive models, addressing limitations of existing techniques. The proposed framework is designed to provide a more adaptable and scalable solution for a wide range of machine learning applications.

title: Adaptive Parameterization Algorithm Based on Quantum Information
abstract: This paper presents an innovative algorithm, the Adaptive Parameterization Algorithm (APA), designed to enhance computational efficiency by dynamically adjusting algorithm parameters based on the target computation and environmental parameters. Utilizing the inherent properties of quantum information, the APA leverages quantum state manipulation to optimize the algorithm's performance in real-time. We introduce a novel mechanism involving quantum state interactions and error correction to achieve this adaptive adjustment. The core claim of this work is that the APA can significantly improve computational throughput compared to traditional parameterization techniques, particularly in complex computational scenarios. This paper details the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness across a range of problems.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF PYTHON PROGRAMMING IN PHARMACY: A REVIEW
authors: Subhajit Samanta*, Dr. Dhrubo, Jyoti Sen
abstract: The growing use of digital technology in healthcare has increased the importance of computational skills in pharmacy. Python is a simple, open-source programming language widely used for data analysis, visualization, modelling, and artificial intelligence. In pharmacy, Python can be applied to pharmacokinetics, pharmaceutical research, drug discovery, formulation development, pharmacovigilance, and clinical data analysis. Introducing basic Python programming into pharmacy education may improve students' analytical abilities and prepare them for modern, technology-driven pharmaceutical research.

title: Feature-Rich Deep Learning Architecture for Breast Cancer Detection: From Image Analysis to Real-Time App Deployment
abstract: Breast cancer would be a major global world concern, particularly among women, for whom early and accurate diagnosis significantly improves treatment outcomes. This paper suggest a feature-rich hybrid deep learning framework that combines traditional handcrafted features, as the Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG), Local Binary Pattern (LBP), Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix, and intensity statistics, with transfer learning models, including ResNet18, ResNet50, and VGG16. These features were fused and classified using a custom multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifier. Among all the tested combinations, GLCM combined with ResNet18 The highest classification accuracy attained on ultrasound breast image data was 89%. The efficacy of the model is substantiated through the application of various evaluation metrics. Furthermore, the model was deployed using StreamLit, enabling real-time clinical inference. The proposed framework continue to support radiologists by offering transparent, interpretable, and reliable computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) tools.

title: Few-shot learning with enhanced calibration for language- and harm-aware multilingual hate speech detection (FLEC-HS)
abstract: Multilingual hate speech detection remains challenging in low-resource settings, where labelled data are limited, particularly for identity-targeted and context-dependent content. We present Few-Shot Learning with Enhanced Calibration for Language- and Harm-Aware Multilingual Hate Speech Detection (FLEC-HS). This modular framework combines few-shot prompting with a frozen GPT-4o model and a lightweight Feature-Conditioned Calibration Layer (FCL) for post-hoc probability calibration. The primary evaluation uses HateDay (approximately 160,000 posts across eight languages), while HateCheck and HateXplain provide complementary functional and cross-dataset diagnostics. The term few-shot refers specifically to the prompting stage, which uses up to K = 16 demonstrations per language. The complete system additionally uses approximately 400 labelled development instances per language to train the FCL and select operating thresholds. Thresholds are selected by five-fold cross-validation on development data and frozen before test evaluation. On HateDay, FLEC-HS achieves a macro-F1 of 0.64, compared with 0.56 for the fully fine-tuned XLM-R-large. At the development-selected operating point requiring hate-class precision of at least 95%, hate recall increases from 0.48 to 0.61. Relative to the fully fine-tuned XLM-R-large baseline (48% review share), FLEC-HS reduces the share of posts sent to human review to 28% under the evaluated entropy-routing policy. Removing the FCL reduces macro-F1 to 0.59 and increases the protected-group false-negative rate from 5.1 to 10.4%. Protected-group fairness is operationalised narrowly through false-negative rates derived from dataset metadata; no broader fairness guarantee is claimed. The findings are limited to the evaluated benchmarks and configuration and remain subject to domain shift, commercial API dependencies, and incomplete coverage of dialects and protected groups.

title: Application of Attention Mechanisms in Sentiment Analysis
abstract: This chapter offers an in-depth exploration of attention mechanisms and their revolutionary impact on sentiment analysis. It introduces the fundamental principles of attention, including Query-Key-Value interactions, additive and scaled dot-product attention, and the self-attention mechanism. The core role of multi-head self-attention within the Transformer architecture is thoroughly explained. Applications across different tasks are examined in detail: text sentiment classification, aspect-based sentiment analysis, multimodal fusion, and graph-structured data using graph attention networks (GATs). Advanced variants such as sparse attention (Longformer and BigBird) are also discussed. A practical case study on aspect-based sentiment analysis demonstrates the implementation and interpretability benefits of attention mechanisms.

title: Explainable Multimodal Deep Learning Integrating Imaging and Clinical Data for Oral Potentially Malignant Disorder Detection
abstract: Oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) are critical precursors to oral cancer, yet clinical detection remains challenging because of substantial phenotypic heterogeneity and overlap with benign conditions. Although image-based deep learning shows promise for automated screening, visual information alone may be insufficient in real-world settings, where diagnostic decisions also rely on patient-specific risk factors. We developed M2-OPMDNet, a multimodal deep learning framework that integrates co-registered white-light and autofluorescence intraoral images with structured clinical information for OPMD detection. A customized questionnaire was designed to capture clinically relevant risk factors and symptoms in a standardized, reproducible format for integration with image-derived features. Multiple image encoders, including conventional convolutional neural networks and foundation model-based architectures, were evaluated using a prospectively collected dataset reflecting real-world screening conditions. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to quantify feature- and modality-level contributions. M2-OPMDNet achieved an AUC of 0.952, outperforming unimodal approaches and showing improved performance for visually subtle lesions. SHAP analysis demonstrated that structured clinical variables contributed substantially to risk estimation and complemented imaging features. These results demonstrate that explainable multimodal learning combining white-light and autofluorescence imaging with structured clinical data can provide accurate, transparent, and clinically grounded OPMD detection. M2-OPMDNet offers a scalable framework for real-world oral cancer screening and decision support.

title: Parameterised graph theory for tensor networks: entanglement rerouting, structural simplification, and agnostic tomography
abstract: Parameterised graph theory studies how the complexity of graph-theoretic problems depends on structural parameters of the input graph. This perspective has proved useful in analysing tensor-network simulation (Markov and Shi, 2008). Its implications for tensor-network representations and tomography are less well understood. In particular, which graph parameters determine whether a tensor-network state (TNS) admits a tractable matrix product state (MPS) or tree tensor network (TTN) representation, and which control the complexity of learning the state? We address these questions using parameterised graph theory. First, we show that cutwidth and tree-cutwidth bound the bond dimension overhead required to represent a TNS as an MPS or TTN. In the TTN case, tree-cutwidth also bounds the local dimension of the grouped subsystems. The proofs are based on entanglement rerouting, a tensor-network analogue of rerouting information in a classical network. Second, we derive graph-dependent upper bounds on the sample and computational complexity of realisable TNS tomography, with exponents that depend on cutwidth, tree-cutwidth, and a new graph parameter, learning complexity, which we bound in terms of degree and treewidth. We obtain these results by extending the disentangling MPS learner of (Cramer et al., 2010), as analysed further in (Bakshi et al., 2025; Lin et al., 2025), to TTNs and to tensor networks on arbitrary known graphs. Finally, we extend the framework beyond the realisable setting. For an arbitrary input state, our agnostic learner outputs a pure state whose fidelity is within additive error $ε$ of the optimum over tensor-network states on the given graph with a given bond dimension, with explicit graph-dependent bounds on sample and computational complexity.

title: P-CORE: Self-Supervised Surface Consistency for Point-Based Neural Editing
abstract: Advances in neural rendering have enabled high-fidelity multi-view reconstruction of 3D scenes. However, free-form non-rigid shape editing remains a significant challenge. Point-based neural representations are highly desirable for multi-view reconstruction because they lack fixed connectivity, which does not constrain the learned surface topology to that of the initialization. Yet this same property causes point-based representations to struggle with holes and surface discontinuities under large deformations. To address this, we propose a novel self-supervised method to enable point-based representations to adapt to large deformations without requiring ground truth multi-view images of deformed geometry. The key idea is to generate random deformations and to ensure consistency in the predicted surface before and after deformation. In particular, the surface prediction from the deformed point cloud should be the same as the deformation applied to the surface prediction from the original point cloud. We incorporate our approach into attention-based point representations, which differ from splatting-based point representations in their use of a learned interpolation kernel between points as opposed to a Gaussian kernel around each point. This learned interpolation kernel can learn to adapt to large deformations, without requiring addition or removal of points. We show that our framework significantly enhances its robustness to large deformations. Experiments on synthetic geometry editing benchmarks (Neural Editor, Objaverse) demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing point-based methods in zero-shot editing and significantly reduces artifacts. Furthermore, qualitative results on the DTU and Mip-NeRF 360 datasets demonstrate our method's effectiveness on real-world scenes.

title: AI, Quantum Computing and High-Performance Computing
abstract: The intersection of AI, quantum computing (QC) and high-performance computing (HPC) creates a spectrum of opportunities. AI is already enhancing QC by assisting with the design and performance of quantum hardware and algorithms, while QC offers the potential to address limitations in classical AI by, for example, improving machine learning and model training. This CETaS Snapshot Report assesses the near-term opportunities provided by hybrid quantum-classical computing systems, and the implications for national security and prosperity. The report outlines a number of challenges and recommendations for the UK’s integration of QC and HPC systems, calling for an acceleration of efforts in order to avoid falling behind in an area central to the future of supercomputing.

title: Synthesis-based Optimization and Verification of Component-based Systems
abstract: Platform-based design enables high-tech equipment manufacturers to deliver many product variants by configuring reusable hardware/software components, but growing system diversity and long product lifecycles make integration and evolution increasingly costly. Engineers must select and integrate hundreds of components, reason about trade-offs (e.g., performance vs. cost), and repeatedly re-verify functional and non-functional requirements after platform updates. This challenge cannot be solved by adding more engineers, as there is also a growing scarcity of skilled labor. The TechFlex 2025 project investigates how to move from expert-driven, manual configuration and late-stage validation to model-based automation for component-based product families. Concretely, it addresses three research questions: (RQ1) to what extent is it possible to synthesize software configurations from a product (platform) variation tree that satisfy functional requirements, constraints, and performance requirements while optimizing other system qualities such as cost? (RQ2) what defines a (minimal) set of component behaviors and interface specifications needed to generate an executable system model that can be used to validate system flows and performance early, without requiring a complete model of all components? (RQ3) to what extent is it possible to accurately predict the performance of arbitrary product configurations based on incremental insights for individual components gained during development and deployment?As a result of research, the project has delivered the following three key contributions:• Automatic synthesis of product variants based on functionality and con-straints (RQ1): A model-based synthesis methodology that enables synthesis of hi-erarchically decomposed software architectures deployed on complex hardware con-figurations is proposed. It contributes generalized meta-models for software and hardware, as well as a Python-based toolchain for design-space exploration. Evalua-tion using both synthetic and industrial-scale cases indicates feasible runtimes (sec-onds to minutes) and valid synthesized solutions.• Component specification required for early system performance analysis (RQ2): A methodology for generating executable models (mock components) from ComMA interface and component specifications to enable early platform verification (including timing constraints) prior to full software availability. It identifies limitations of reusing trace-based component semantics for code generation and proposes run-to-completion restrictions plus an operational interpretation that supports synthesis. evidence.abstract: Platform-based design enables high-tech equipment manufacturers to deliver many product variants by configuring reusable hardware/software components, but growing system diversity and long product lifecycles make integration and evolution increasingly costly. title: Probability Topological Simulation for Dynamic Gradient Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic gradient optimization algorithm based on probability topological simulation. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with complex, high-dimensional problems, requiring extensive manual parameter tuning. This approach leverages probabilistic topological simulation to dynamically adjust the structure of a system, enabling the exploration of a wider range of potential solutions. We propose a framework where a probabilistic topology map is generated, and the optimization process iteratively refines this map based on a predefined objective function. This iterative refinement guides the algorithm towards solutions that exhibit higher complexity and potential complexity. The core mechanism involves a continuous evaluation of the resulting topology map, allowing the algorithm to automatically optimize the parameters to achieve the desired outcome. This paper explores the advantages of this approach compared to traditional methods, particularly in handling complex, multi-dimensional problems. We present preliminary results demonstrating the effectiveness of this technique in a specific, challenging optimization scenario.

title: 基于拓扑结构的数据压缩与编码
abstract: This paper explores the application of topology-based compression and encoding techniques for data reduction and storage. Traditional data compression methods often fail to fully exploit the inherent structural properties of data, hindering efficiency and storage utilization. We propose a novel approach that leverages topology to identify and exploit these structural characteristics, resulting in a more effective compression and encoding process. The core mechanism centers around constructing a mapping that reflects the underlying topology of the data, enabling intelligent data representation and efficient encoding. This research aims to enhance data transfer efficiency and storage space through a fundamentally new approach to data representation. The paper presents a preliminary investigation of the proposed methodology, demonstrating its potential to yield significant improvements in data compression ratios compared to existing techniques.

title: Title: Predictive Chaos Dynamics with Bayesian Stochastic Filtering
abstract: Predictive chaos dynamics, the ability to forecast the trajectory of chaotic systems, remains a significant challenge in complex systems modeling. Traditional approaches often rely on historical data, limiting their ability to capture the inherent uncertainty within chaotic systems. This paper proposes a novel dynamic Bayesian stochastic filtering (DSBF) algorithm designed to overcome these limitations by explicitly modeling the probability of future states, incorporating an evolving Bayesian prior. We argue that focusing solely on past observations is insufficient for accurate forecasting in chaotic systems; instead, the algorithm leverages the system's inherent uncertainty to provide highly predictive capabilities. This work introduces a dynamically updated prior based on observed trends, resulting in improved forecasting accuracy and a fundamental shift towards probabilistic forecasting. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through extensive simulations and analysis of chaotic system trajectories.

title: 基于生物拓扑的量子计算算法优化
abstract: Abstract: Quantum computing, a revolutionary paradigm in computation, holds immense potential across diverse fields, including drug discovery, materials science, and cryptography. However, realizing this potential faces significant challenges, primarily due to the inherent complexity of quantum algorithms and their sensitivity to subtle variations. This paper investigates a novel quantum computing algorithm optimization framework based on biological topology, aiming to enhance the efficiency of quantum computations. We introduce a framework leveraging the unique structural properties of biological networks to guide the optimization process, resulting in improved performance compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around identifying and utilizing specific topological patterns within biological data to inform the design of quantum circuits. This approach promises to overcome limitations of existing optimization techniques by introducing a fundamentally different perspective on algorithm design. The study explores the potential of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, demonstrating its effectiveness in optimizing specific quantum circuit designs. This research contributes to the development of robust and adaptable optimization strategies for quantum computing, paving the way for more efficient and scalable quantum systems.

title: 基于贝叶斯网络的多模态信息融合框架
abstract: This paper presents a Bayesian network-based multi-modal information fusion framework designed to enhance the accuracy and robustness of fusion processes. The framework addresses the inherent uncertainties and correlations present in multi-modal data by dynamically adjusting fusion weights based on these characteristics. The core mechanism leverages Bayesian networks to probabilistically model each modality and employs information-theoretic measures, specifically entropy and mutual information, to quantify the relationships between modalities. This allows for adaptive weighting schemes, providing a more robust and accurate fusion outcome compared to traditional methods reliant on fixed rules or statistical learning. The framework's novelty lies in its dynamic modeling of modality relationships, offering a flexible approach to complex multi-modal data integration.

title: Quantum State Geometries for Quantum Computing Simulation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of non-linear geometric transformations to quantum states to construct simulation environments for quantum computing. The core claim is that by manipulating the geometric structure of quantum states, we can achieve higher simulation accuracy and efficiency compared to traditional methods. This research explores a novel approach to generating complex geometric representations of quantum states, utilizing these representations to enhance the fidelity of quantum simulations. The paper details a method for creating a non-linear transformation that converts a quantum state into a complex geometric structure, and details how this structure is exploited to facilitate accurate simulations. The study focuses on the potential for this geometric approach to overcome limitations of existing simulation techniques.

title: Cognitive Architectures for Embodied AI with Bayesian Inference
abstract: This paper proposes a novel cognitive architecture for embodied artificial intelligence (AI) systems, designed to address the limitations of current approaches. The architecture leverages principles of cognitive science, specifically Bayesian inference, hierarchical control, and reinforcement learning, to facilitate robust learning and adaptation within complex, dynamic environments. The core claim is that existing embodied AI systems lack a holistic cognitive architecture capable of seamlessly integrating perception, action, and learning. The developed architecture aims to overcome this deficiency by providing a structured framework for representing knowledge, planning actions, and updating beliefs based on sensory input and interaction. Key components include a Bayesian inference engine for probabilistic reasoning, a hierarchical control system for managing complex behaviors, and reinforcement learning algorithms for optimizing actions and achieving goals. This integrated approach promises to significantly enhance the capabilities of embodied AI agents, enabling them to navigate, learn, and interact with the world in a more intelligent and adaptive manner. The architecture is presented as a modular system, allowing for flexibility and extensibility as the field of embodied AI continues to evolve. This document outlines the architectural design, the underlying principles, and the anticipated benefits of this approach.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Storage Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed storage protocol leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance security and resilience against attacks. Traditional distributed storage systems rely on classical cryptographic algorithms, which are vulnerable to advances in computing power and algorithmic breakthroughs. This protocol aims to mitigate these vulnerabilities by directly exploiting the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum entanglement, for secure data storage and retrieval. The core idea is to establish entangled states between storage nodes. Data encryption and verification are then performed by manipulating these entangled states, eliminating the need for conventional key exchange processes. This approach offers a fundamentally different security paradigm, providing a higher level of confidentiality and resistance against attacks that target classical cryptographic assumptions. The protocol's efficiency and scalability will be explored conceptually, laying the groundwork for future research and potential implementation.

title: Evolutionary Symbolic Program Generation and Verification
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program generation and verification by integrating evolutionary algorithms with symbolic execution techniques. The core idea is to leverage the search capabilities of evolutionary algorithms to discover optimal program representations (symbols) and then employ symbolic program generation to translate these symbols into executable code. Crucially, formal verification methods are applied to ensure the correctness of the generated code. The system automates a traditionally manual and often error-prone process, significantly enhancing both efficiency and reliability. We demonstrate the feasibility and potential of this combined approach through a detailed explanation of the methodology and theoretical underpinnings. The resulting system offers a pathway towards automated software development and verification, particularly for complex systems where manual design and exhaustive testing are impractical.

title: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy and Personalized Model Aggregation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising approach to training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, traditional FL methods are vulnerable to information leakage and model divergence, particularly when dealing with highly heterogeneous client datasets. This research proposes a novel framework that combines differential privacy (DP) with personalized model aggregation (PMA) to mitigate these issues. The core claim is that integrating DP safeguards client data while PMA allows for adaptation of the global model to individual client characteristics. We introduce a rigorous methodology for quantifying the trade-offs between privacy, model accuracy, and computational overhead. The proposed approach enhances both the robustness and effectiveness of FL systems, paving the way for more secure and adaptable distributed learning applications. Specifically, we formulate the aggregation process using the following notation: Let $m_i$ represent the model received from client *i*, $s_i$ be the local data used by client *i*, and $\epsilon$ and $\delta$ be the privacy parameters. The personalized aggregation function is defined as: $m_{aggregated} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{K} \alpha_i * m_i}{\sum_{i=1}^{K} \alpha_i}$ where $\alpha_i$ are weights determined based on client data characteristics and privacy constraints. We leverage differential privacy by adding noise to the model updates, represented as: $m_i' = m_i + \epsilon * N(0, I_d)$ where $N(0, I_d)$ denotes Gaussian noise with mean 0 and covariance matrix $I_d$ (d-dimensional identity matrix).

title: Hierarchical Latent Variable Discovery via Bayesian Deep Belief Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for hierarchical latent variable discovery within complex datasets leveraging Bayesian Deep Belief Networks (BDBNs). The core challenge in latent variable discovery lies in both the dimensionality of the problem and the inherent ambiguity in interpreting the discovered factors. Traditional methods often struggle with scalability and providing meaningful explanations for the identified latent structures. Our approach addresses these limitations by employing a deep belief network architecture with explicitly modeled hierarchical layers, combined with Bayesian inference to quantify uncertainty. This allows us to not only identify groupings of latent variables but also to assess their reliability. The resulting representations are expected to be more interpretable and robust. We propose a framework for training BDBNs with a hierarchical structure, incorporating prior knowledge and utilizing variational inference to estimate the posterior distribution over the latent variables. This approach offers a significant improvement over standard deep learning methods in terms of interpretability and uncertainty quantification, ultimately leading to more actionable insights from complex data. The methodology presented here facilitates the automatic construction of hierarchical latent variable models, promoting a deeper understanding of underlying data patterns.

title: Quantum System Self-Adaptive Noise Parameter Adjustment
abstract: Quantum system noise represents a significant challenge to achieving precise control and optimization in quantum computation. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive algorithm for quantum system noise parameter adjustment, designed to dynamically adjust noise parameters based on the system's inherent dynamic behavior. The core mechanism leverages a feedback loop that continuously monitors and responds to noise fluctuations, ensuring stability and accuracy throughout the quantum process. This approach offers a significant improvement over static parameter adjustment methods, enabling more robust and adaptable control over quantum systems. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through simulations, showcasing its ability to maintain coherence and achieve targeted quantum operations with reduced sensitivity to noise fluctuations.

We demonstrate that our approach, utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition, dynamically adjusts the simulation's resolution based on input data, resulting in significantly improved accuracy and reduced computational cost for turbulent flows. The core mechanism involves manipulating the quantum state of a simplified fluid element to effectively represent the complex flow pattern, offering a scalable and efficient alternative to traditional methods. The potential impact of this work is a shift towards more accurate and computationally feasible turbulence modeling.

title: Quantum Topologies for Adaptive Quantum Computing
abstract: Quantum Topologies offer a novel approach to quantum computation, leveraging the intricate properties of quantum geometry to create highly resilient and adaptable quantum systems. This paper investigates a framework for adaptive quantum computation based on quantum topology, focusing on the design of an algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters based on input data. We propose a method for generating and manipulating quantum states using topological properties, demonstrating its potential to overcome limitations of conventional quantum computing. The core mechanism centers around the application of topological invariants to guide quantum state evolution, leading to enhanced computational performance. This work presents a conceptual design and preliminary results exploring the feasibility of this approach, highlighting the advantages of quantum topology in achieving more efficient and robust quantum computation.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Operational Intelligence: A Technical Architecture for AI-Powered Field Service Automation
abstract: This paper presents a technical architecture for AI-powered operational intelligence in field service management, as implemented in FieldMind AI (GFM). The architecture combines workflow orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounded in a vector-indexed operational knowledge base, and a multi-channel communication gateway into a unified system capable of interpreting operational signals — chemical readings, equipment alerts, inventory levels — and generating context-aware, prioritized responses. We describe each architectural layer, the design rationale behind key technical choices, and trade-offs relevant to deploying this class of system for small and independent field service businesses.

title: Deep Learning in Multimodal Breast Cancer Imaging: From Image Reconstruction and Segmentation to Diagnosis and Treatment Response Prediction
abstract: Breast cancer imaging is central to screening, diagnosis, staging, treatment monitoring, and post-treatment surveillance, but image interpretation remains limited by variable image quality, interobserver variability, false-positive findings and heterogeneous tumor biology. This narrative review summarizes current applications of deep learning in multimodal breast cancer imaging, with emphasis on image reconstruction, image enhancement, lesion detection, segmentation, classification, biomarker prediction, treatment response assessment, prognosis and clinical implementation. A structured literature search was performed across major biomedical and technical databases, focusing on studies involving mammography, digital breast tomosynthesis, ultrasound, MRI, PET/CT, digital pathology and multimodal fusion approaches. Current evidence indicates that deep learning can support image denoising; super-resolution, low-dose, and accelerated reconstruction; lesion localization; tumor segmentation; benign–malignant classification; and molecular or biomarker-related prediction. Multimodal models integrating radiological imaging, histopathology, clinical variables, and molecular markers show particular promise for treatment response prediction, recurrence risk estimation, and personalized decision support. However, clinical translation remains limited by retrospective study designs, small and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, inconsistent annotations, limited explainability, bias, lack of prospective validation, and regulatory challenges. Deep learning should therefore be viewed as a decision-support framework that may improve breast cancer imaging workflows if validated in diverse, prospective, and clinically representative settings.

title: A Resource-Efficient End-to-End Multimodal AI Framework for Automated PET-CT Report Generation and TNM Staging in Breast Cancer
abstract: Objectives: Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography (PET-CT) is integral to breast cancer staging. However, manual interpretation is time-consuming and subject to inter-observer variability. While artificial intelligence has shown promise in lesion detection and standardised uptake value (SUVmax) quantification, existing approaches are fragmented and do not generate complete TNM-aligned structured reports. Consequently, there remains a need for an integrated framework capable of translating PET-CT data into structured clinical reports. Material and Methods: We developed a Multimodal Report Generator (MMRG) as an exploratory pilot study using data from 85 breast cancer patients (439 clusters; 59/15/11 train/validation/test). The framework combines tri-planar Swin3D feature extraction, multimodal feature fusion, multi-task lesion analysis, and (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) GPT-2-based report generation with Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) retrieval-augmented generation. The entire pipeline was trained on a single consumer-grade graphics processing unit (GPU), supporting a resource-efficient design. Results: Model Training demonstrated stable convergence without evidence of train-validation divergence. At the selected validation checkpoint (15 patients, 50 clusters), lesion detection achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.861 and an F1 score of 0.757, while descriptor classification achieved a ROC-AUC of 0.787 and an F1 score of 0.757. SUVmax and lesion-size estimation showed Pearson correlations of 0.44 and 0.64, respectively. On the held-out internal test set ( n = 11 patients, 61 clusters), lesion detection achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.857, an F1 score of 0.652, and a Cohen’s κ of 0.466, while descriptor classification achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.759, an F1 score of 0.546, and a κ of 0.381. Quantitative estimation yielded SUVmax mean absolute error (MAE) = 6.44 (Pearson r = 0.49) and lesion-size MAE = 0.73 cm (Pearson r = 0.34). Tumour-Node-Metastasis (TNM) staging accuracy was 18.2%, with M-stage accuracy of 63.6%. The organ-domain hallucination rate was 35.7% on breast-cancer-relevant test clusters. The framework successfully generated structured PET-CT reports with automated lesion description and TNM staging. Conclusion: This exploratory pilot study demonstrates the feasibility of an end-to-end multimodal AI pipeline for PET-CT interpretation in breast cancer, combining lesion detection, quantitative measurement, structured report generation, and TNM staging within a single framework. While lesion- and descriptor-classification showed encouraging performance, TNM staging results remain preliminary in this small cohort. The framework is presented as a resource-efficient prototype for future larger-cohort studies rather than a clinically validated deployment-ready system. Future work will focus on larger multi-centre datasets, improved quantitative estimation, and direct or joint TNM-stage prediction architectures.

title: Автоматизированная контент генерация в SMM на B2B рынке информационных технологий
abstract: Целью работы является создание, обучение и оценка эффективности специализированного программного инструмента для автоматизированной генерации B2B-контента на базе больших языковых моделей (LLM). Методология проведения работы включает теоретический анализ предметной области, методы сбора и предварительной обработки естественного языка, семантический обратный инжиниринг, а также методы эффективного дообучения нейронных сетей (QLoRA, SFT, IPO) и автоматизированной оценки качества текстов с использованием парадигмы LLM-as-a-Judge. В ходе работы получены следующие основные результаты: сформирован репрезентативный датасет из 40 000 публикаций ИТ-компаний в Telegram; произведено дообучение языковой модели Gemma-4; реализован полноценный вычислительный конвейер генерации контента. Сравнительный анализ показал, что модель, прошедшая этап SFT, демонстрирует наивысшую эффективность при создании глубоких технических гайдов, тогда как базовая модель лучше справляется с форматом классических кейс-стади. Областью применения результатов работы являются маркетинговые отделы и SMM-агентства, специализирующиеся на продвижении продуктов и услуг в корпоративном секторе (B2B ИТ). Внедрение разработанного инструмента на базе LLM решает проблему «бутылочного горлышка» технической экспертизы в ИТ-маркетинге. Использование дообученной модели позволяет делегировать искусственному интеллекту перевод сложной инженерной информации на язык профессионального маркетинга, что снижает удельные затраты на производство контента и повышает рентабельность маркетинговых инвестиций без потери фактологической точности.

title: LentEx: Generalizable Latent Entity Extraction via Synthetic Data and Instruction-Tuned LLMs
abstract: Latent entity extraction (LEE) tackles the challenge of identifying implicit, contextually inferred entities within free text-an area where traditional entity extraction methods fall short. In this paper, we introduce LentEx, a novel framework for latent entity extraction that leverages synthetic data generation and instruction fine-tuning to optimize smaller, efficient large language models (LLMs). Latent entities, which are often abstract and thematic, are crucial for applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), customer persona analysis, and knowledge graph enrichment. LentEx addresses the scarcity of labeled datasets by employing a template-based approach to generate diverse, contextually rich synthetic data, ensuring high variability and alignment with real-world distributions. To our knowledge, LentEx is the first to systematically approach LEE through the lens of LLMs. LentEx demonstrates significant performance improvements across multiple tasks, notably surpassing state-of-the-art models on the MTEB Clustering Benchmark. Furthermore, our methodology enables robust generalization to unseen domains, making LentEx highly applicable in real-world NLP tasks, including RAG and clustering, thereby establishing a new paradigm for latent entity understanding and extraction in natural language processing.

title: SENTINEL-RL: Offloading Topological Reasoning from LLM Agents in the Security Operations Center
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly proposed as autonomous SOC analysts, but two limitations make them unreliable at enterprise scale: a finite context window cannot hold a multi-thousand-host authentication graph, and free-form generation offers no guarantee that a recommended containment action is consistent with the topology it operates on. We present Sentinel-RL, an agentic-SOC architecture that decouples topological reasoning from semantic reasoning: a heterogeneous graph attention encoder summarizes the live authentication subgraph into a fixed-dimensional state, a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy maps this state to a constrained set of investigative actions, and an LLM agent loop is restricted to consuming the policy's recommendations and producing analyst-readable narratives gated by a critic. We instantiate the system on the LANL Comprehensive, Multi-Source Cyber-Security Events dataset and the Indiana University Quartz HPC cluster, reporting four results: (i) a two-phase CREATE ingestion pattern loads a 24M-edge authentication subgraph into Neo4j in 14.2 minutes on a single 32-core node, roughly 24x faster than the canonical MERGE-based pipeline; (ii) a sliding-window alert engine reliably trips a 25-event/10-second threshold in <=2.5 s across 50 trials; (iii) PPO training over 200 iterations converges to a mean episodic return of 8.74+/-0.31, with held-out precision of 0.91 and recall of 0.87 on labeled red-team events; and (iv) the integrated containment loop completes a full detect-investigate-recommend-human-approve cycle in a median of 6.3 s. We contribute a reusable engineering pattern (the hot-node deadlock workaround), a portable HPC deployment pattern (anchor-node co-location), and an enterprise-readiness analysis covering false-positive economics, reversibility guarantees, audit compliance, and the human-approval boundary.

title: Bayesian Spectral Decomposition for Differential Geometry
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Spectral Decomposition (BSD) algorithm for geometric object representation and evolution. Traditional methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the flexibility and adaptability of geometric models. BSD leverages a probabilistic framework, updating posterior distributions of geometric object parameters as new data is observed. The algorithm efficiently captures complex geometric shapes and allows for accurate prediction of their evolution. We present a detailed theoretical analysis and practical implementation of the algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness through simulations and a simplified case study. This approach offers a robust and adaptable representation for geometric modeling, reducing the need for extensive parameter tuning. The core mechanism lies in iteratively refining the posterior distribution of geometric object parameters using Bayesian inference, enabling the algorithm to handle complex geometries and provide accurate predictions.

title: Title: Hierarchical Bayesian Model for Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper presents a novel hierarchical Bayesian model designed to address the challenges inherent in modeling dynamical systems. Traditional approaches often struggle with accurately capturing long-term dependencies and the intricate relationships between variables at different levels of granularity. Our model leverages Bayesian inference to dynamically update state probabilities, creating a nested hierarchy that facilitates more precise prediction and enhanced understanding of system behavior. We introduce a framework for representing states as a hierarchical structure, enabling the modeling of dependencies across multiple scales. The core mechanism involves iteratively refining state probabilities based on observed data, fostering a more robust and adaptable representation of the system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations exploring various dynamical systems, highlighting its ability to improve long-term forecasting accuracy compared to existing methods.

title: 基于自适应的分布式量子计算算法优化框架
abstract: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) offers immense potential for tackling complex computational problems, but its realization faces significant challenges related to algorithm design, parameter optimization, and scalability. This paper proposes a novel algorithm optimization framework for DQC, centered around a dynamically adaptive quantum state self-adaptation mechanism. The framework leverages the inherent complexity of DQC to automatically adjust quantum parameters, ultimately enhancing the precision and efficiency of computations while enabling support for large-scale quantum systems. We introduce a mechanism to continuously monitor and adjust parameters based on the quantum state, leading to improved performance characteristics. This work addresses the limitations of existing optimization techniques and paves the way for more robust and efficient DQC systems. The core mechanism focuses on a self-tuning approach, dynamically adjusting the quantum state based on the current computation, thereby optimizing performance. This research presents a framework that can dynamically adjust parameters, improving the overall quality of computations.

title: Nonlinear Topological Structures in Adaptive Quantum Information Coding
abstract: Quantum information is a fundamental resource in modern technology, demanding robust security measures. Traditional quantum information encoding methods often fall short in this regard, particularly when security is paramount. This paper investigates the application of non-linear topological structures to adaptive quantum information encoding, exploring a novel approach that leverages dynamic adjustments to the topology to enhance both the fidelity and security of quantum information transmission. We propose a mechanism that utilizes a self-adaptive topology to dynamically adjust the encoding parameters, ensuring optimal performance against potential attacks. The core claim is that this design significantly improves quantum information security through enhanced robustness and adaptability.

This paper investigates the application of non-linear topological structures to adaptive quantum information encoding, exploring a novel approach that leverages dynamic adjustments to the topology to enhance both the fidelity and security of quantum information transmission. title: Autonomous Theorem Proving with Neural Network-Guided Search
abstract: This paper explores the potential of integrating neural networks into the process of autonomous theorem proving to significantly improve efficiency. Traditional autonomous theorem provers often struggle with combinatorial explosion, leading to prolonged proof search times. This work proposes a novel approach where a neural network is trained to predict the most promising proof strategies given the current state of the proof process. The network's predictive capabilities aim to guide the theorem prover's search, focusing computational resources on potentially fruitful avenues. We outline the core components of this system, detailing the neural network architecture, training methodology, and integration strategy with a standard theorem proving framework. The key contribution lies in the ability of a machine learning model to learn and adapt to the specific nuances of a given proof task, offering a dynamic and potentially far more efficient approach to automated reasoning compared to traditional, rule-based search algorithms. The presented framework represents a step toward creating truly intelligent theorem provers capable of tackling complex mathematical problems with increased speed and reliability.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Reinforcement Learning with Latent State Representations
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) in conjunction with latent state representations for reinforcement learning (RL). Traditional RL methods often struggle with exploration, generalization, and robustness, particularly in complex and partially observable environments. We propose a novel framework where the environment's state is modeled as a distribution over latent states, and a PPL is employed to define the agent's policy and value function. This approach enables Bayesian inference, allowing the agent to quantify uncertainty and improve exploration strategies. Furthermore, leveraging latent representations facilitates generalization by capturing underlying structure within the state space. The core claim of this work is that this combined approach significantly enhances exploration, generalization, and robustness in RL. We outline the key components of this framework and discuss the benefits of incorporating PPLs for improved learning performance, emphasizing the ability to reason about uncertainty and adapt to novel situations. The methodology presented offers a promising direction for developing more sophisticated and reliable RL agents.

title: Self-Organizing Topological Quantum Computing Simulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum computing simulation leveraging the principles of self-organization in topological quantum matter. We develop a simulation tool, termed "Topological Echo Simulation" (TES), designed to emulate complex quantum phenomena, including topological order, spin configuration, and entanglement, by mimicking the self-organizing behavior of topological phases. The TES utilizes a modified quantum state representation to accurately represent and simulate the evolution of these topological structures. The core mechanism involves generating and manipulating a highly complex, dynamically evolving quantum state, guided by a carefully designed topological algorithm, which produces a topologically robust and coherent simulation. The paper details the TES's architecture, the underlying mathematical framework, and the simulation process, highlighting its potential for advanced quantum simulation and its contribution to the exploration of quantum topological physics. The focus is on demonstrating the tool's capabilities through illustrative examples and preliminary results focusing on the simulation of a simple topological phase, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed method.

title: Non-Euclidean Constraint Optimization with Dynamic Topology (NCO-DT)
abstract: This paper introduces Non-Euclidean Constraint Optimization with Dynamic Topology (NCO-DT), a novel approach to complex optimization problems. Traditional optimization methods often struggle with high-dimensional spaces and intricate structural dependencies, leading to suboptimal solutions. NCO-DT addresses this challenge by employing a dynamically adaptive topology, allowing the system to reformulate itself based on real-time assessment of the problem's characteristics. This adaptation facilitates the exploration of a broader solution space and enhances the robustness of the optimization process. The core mechanism centers around a 'Adaptive Topology Mapping' algorithm, which iteratively refines the system's geometry while maintaining the objective function's constraints. We demonstrate the effectiveness of NCO-DT through a series of case studies involving diverse optimization challenges, showcasing its ability to surpass conventional methods in terms of solution quality and computational efficiency.

title: Self-Organizing Neural Networks for Robot Navigation in Dynamic Environments
abstract: This paper investigates the application of self-organizing neural networks (SOMs) to robot navigation within dynamic environments. Traditional robot navigation often relies on explicit programming or reinforcement learning, which can be challenging to implement and adapt to unforeseen changes. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing SOMs to enable robots to autonomously learn and execute navigation strategies. The core idea is to map the environment into a self-organized structure, where neurons representing different regions adapt to the robot's surroundings through proximity and interaction. This eliminates the need for predefined rules and allows the robot to dynamically adjust its behavior in response to changing conditions. The paper details the SOM architecture, the learning process, and the resulting navigation capabilities. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to achieve robust and adaptive navigation in complex, dynamic scenarios.

title: 基于拓扑的神经网络 (Topological Neural Networks)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed Topological Neural Networks (TNNs), that leverages the inherent topological structure of data to enhance model generalization and robustness. Traditional neural networks often fail to effectively capture the underlying data patterns, while TNNs aim to exploit this structure for improved performance. The core mechanism involves mapping network weights and connections to the topology of the data, thereby facilitating the learning of relevant features through the structure itself. This research explores the potential of utilizing topological properties to mitigate overfitting and improve the model's ability to generalize to unseen data. The paper details the design of TNNs, their training methodology, and experimental results demonstrating their improved performance compared to conventional neural networks on several benchmark datasets.

title: Title: Geometric Formalism for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric formalism for multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) systems, aiming to enhance the stability and interpretability of algorithms. Traditional MARL approaches often struggle with complex interactions and the difficulty in understanding the decision-making processes within these systems. We propose a framework that represents agent interactions as geometric graphs, explicitly modeling proximity, connectivity, and preferential paths. This geometric representation allows for a more intuitive and structured analysis of the system's dynamics, facilitating the identification of critical decision points and potential convergence issues. The paper details the implementation of this geometric formalism, explores its impact on algorithm performance, and discusses potential future directions for research. The core claim is that this geometric approach significantly improves the robustness and interpretability of MARL systems, offering a shift towards a more formalized and comprehensible approach to complex decision-making.

title: Quantum State Vector Reconstruction via Bayesian Inference
abstract: Quantum state vector reconstruction is a fundamental problem in quantum information theory, crucial for tasks like quantum state tomography and quantum error correction. Traditional methods often struggle with noisy measurements and lack a principled framework for uncertainty quantification. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum State Vector Reconstruction via Bayesian Inference, that leverages Bayesian inference to reconstruct a quantum state vector from a set of measurements, enhancing accuracy and offering a more robust approach compared to existing methods. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the integration of Bayesian estimation for uncertainty quantification and refinement of the reconstruction process. The algorithm incorporates a probabilistic approach to estimate the state vector distribution, improving reconstruction by incorporating uncertainty estimates directly into the reconstruction process. This results in a more reliable and accurate state vector reconstruction, particularly when dealing with noisy measurements. This work addresses the limitations of conventional methods by providing a principled Bayesian framework for state vector reconstruction, offering a significant advancement in this field.

title: Title: Non-Linear Topological Maps for Data Compression
abstract: This paper explores the application of novel non-linear topological maps for data compression. Traditional compression techniques often rely on discrete data representations and can struggle with complex data. We propose a new class of topological maps, designed to dynamically adapt to the data's structure, offering superior compression ratios compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a self-replicating topology that intelligently expands and contracts to represent the data, leveraging a sparse encoding scheme. This approach aims to create a 'compressed' representation that minimizes redundancy while maintaining data integrity. We detail the mathematical framework of this approach, including the defining topological space, the self-replicating element, and the encoding process. The paper concludes with a discussion of the experimental results demonstrating the effectiveness of this new method, highlighting its potential for significant improvements in data compression.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel Quantum Adaptive Time Series Prediction (QATSP) algorithm, designed to enhance prediction accuracy by dynamically adjusting model parameters based on historical data. title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Interdisciplinary Mapping Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Betwixt
abstract: Semantic knowledge is commonly represented in structures designed for persistence, exchange, or machine reasoning, while human review and much data-processing software operate more naturally on rectangular data. This paper introduces Betwixt, an R implementation of reviewable relational projections for semantic assertions. Betwixt treats atomic subject–predicate–value assertions as independently identifiable semantic units and projects them into tidy long or wider relational forms appropriate to particular review operations. Dual projections additionally align an assertion with another assertion establishing its relationship to evidentiary material, without combining the two into a compound semantic assertion. The resulting representations provide an intermediate layer between semantic models and human-centred review interfaces. The paper distinguishes projection from review semantics, describes the principal projection classes supported by the Betwixt model, and demonstrates their use in constructing reproducible review workspaces while preserving the identities required for subsequent provenance-aware semantic processing.

title: Использование AI – технологий в индустрии туризма и гостеприимства для продвижения туристской дестинации на внутреннем рынке (на примере Республики Карелия)
abstract: Данная работа посвящена разработке AI-ассистента для продвижения туристкой дестинации Республики Карелия. В процессе исследования были решены следующие задачи: 1. Изучение мировых и отечественных практик применения искусственного интеллекта для продвижения туристкой дестинации 2. Исследование рынка туристических услуг Республики Карелия 3. Выявление основных проблем развития и организации туристкой индустрии в рамках объекта исследования 4. Разработка AI-ассистента на основе отечественной LLM 5. Разработка комплекса мер в сфере AI для решения проблем продвижения Республики Карелия как туристкой дестинации на внутреннем рынке туризма В ходе работы были рассмотрены основные практики применения искусственного интеллекта в сфере туризма, их преимущества и недостатки. Были выявлены основные проблемы Республики Карелия в сфере развития и организации туристкой индустрии. Результатом работы стала разработка для Республики Карелия комплекса мер в сфере AI для решения проблем продвижения Республики как туристкой дестинации на внутреннем рынке туризма, а также разработка AI-ассистента на основе данных решений. Для достижения данных результатов в работе были использованы/разработаны следующие информационные технологии, в том числе программное обеспечение, облачные сервисы, базы данных и прочие: текстовый, графический редактор и электронные таблицы.

title: XAI Decoded
abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) aims to close that gap by producing human-understandable outputs that establish trust, transparency, and accountability between people and AI systems. This chapter provides a systematic literature review (SLR), according to PRISMA, to analyze peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2024. The review also differentiates between local and global explanation methods in terms of whether they concentrate on individual predictions or on general model behavior. Based on our findings, SHAP and LIME are overwhelmingly used in practice because they work with black-box models and are easy to implement, although the two methods differ in their theoretical foundation and computational complexity. Despite the increasing relevance of XAI in safety-critical areas such as healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, open issues remain concerning the sacrifice of interpretability in favor of accuracy, the absence of standardized evaluation metrics, and human-focused design.

title: Introduction
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive foundation for the entire book by introducing the core concepts, scope, and significance of sentiment analysis in natural language processing. It begins with an overview of sentiment analysis as a key subfield that extracts subjective information from textual, audio, and visual data. The chapter systematically defines sentiment analysis, explores its three primary modalities (textual, audio, and visual), and outlines its expanded scope, including multimodal analysis, industry-specific applications, real-time processing, cross-cultural challenges, and ethical concerns. It further discusses the growing importance of sentiment analysis in business intelligence, public safety, public health, finance, politics, and e-commerce, supported by a detailed table of applications across domains. The historical evolution, research significance, current challenges, and future directions are also examined. Finally, the chapter presents the overall structure of the book, describing how each subsequent chapter builds upon the previous ones to guide readers from foundational concepts to advanced techniques and practical applications.

title: A Semantic Model of Genetic Evidence: A Step Toward Bridging the Basic-Science-Clinic Gap
abstract: Scientific and clinical decision-making depends on evidence from the primary literature, but existing standards for representing that evidence (FHIR Evidence, ECO, SEPIO, and the GA4GH Genomic Knowledge Standards) are oriented toward clinical-trial workflows, evidence codes, or single-variant assertions, and do not capture the fine-grained, domain-specific structure of claims in basic and pre-clinical research. We introduce a semantic model for scientific evidence with three core classes, specialize it for genetics, align it structurally to FHIR Evidence with a SEPIO-anchored credibility decomposition, and attach a compact dimensional vocabulary whose conditional-activation rules are validated by a SHACL schema for the implemented constraints. Using clinical variant interpretation as the driving use case, we evaluate the model through a human-AI annotation pilot over six genetics papers, yielding 28 evidence items and 95 source-anchored assertions, with a workflow that keeps curator-authored reference annotations distinct from AI-drafted annotations. Treating the pilot as a feasibility study rather than a benchmark, we argue that the model is a useful increment toward trustworthy, AI-ready infrastructure for variant interpretation: a reference data model and validation schema for representing genetic evidence.

title: Persistent Identity Preservation in Generative Image Models: A Benchmark and Evaluation System
abstract: Generative image models can now produce high-quality images, follow complex instructions, and support precise edits, but they still struggle to preserve who or what is being depicted. When generating or editing images of a specific subject, identity may drift as the pose, expression, appearance, viewpoint, or surrounding scene changes. Existing subject-driven methods make fundamentally different choices about where identity is represented: through the input context (GPT-Image-2, NB2), as trainable subject-specific model parameters (LoRA), or as a persistent identity layer (PHOTA IDENTITY) reusable across generations and edits. We systematically benchmark these paradigms across subject-driven generation, editing, restoration, and multi-subject settings, with tasks designed to increasingly stress identity preservation. Our results show that identity preservation remains a distinct limitation of current generative foundation models: strong image quality and instruction following do not necessarily imply strong identity fidelity, and identity degradation becomes more pronounced under iterative edits, small subject scales, severe image degradation, and multi-subject composition. Persistent identity substantially reduces this degradation across generation, editing, and restoration, consistently improving identity preservation when applied to different foundation models while maintaining comparable instruction adherence and perceptual image quality. These results suggest that identity does not simply emerge from increasingly capable generative models, but can instead be represented as persistent subject knowledge that is composed independently with the underlying generative model.

title: Well-posedness of Filtering Equations in Weighted Sobolev Spaces with Unbounded System Coefficients
abstract: Nonlinear filtering problem is one of the core subjects in modern control theory. In this paper, we will study the well-posedness of the three fundamental evolution equations arising in continuous-time nonlinear filtering--the robust Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, the stochastic DMZ equation, and the Kushner-Stratonovich equation--within a unified buffered weighted formulation. An exponential-type weight function and the corresponding weighted Sobolev spaces are introduced to enable a variational treatment of the filtering equations in a more general setting, in which the coefficients of the filtering system may be unbounded with polynomial growth. Under mild and easily verifiable assumptions, we first establish the well-posedness of the weak solution to the robust DMZ equation in these weighted spaces. Using the gauge (exponential) transformation and its inverse, these results are then transferred to the stochastic DMZ equation and the Kushner-Stratonovich equation, whose solutions are shown to exist and be unique in buffered weighted Sobolev spaces, yielding a unified treatment of all three filtering equations. Sufficient conditions for the well-posedness are also summarized, which illustrate the wide applicability of the proposed framework to general nonlinear filtering systems.

title: Adaptive Quantum Loop
abstract: This paper introduces a novel computational framework, the Adaptive Quantum Loop, designed to precisely model quantum system evolution through dynamic parameter adjustment. Traditional approaches often rely on empirical tuning, while our framework leverages a robust parameter adjustment mechanism to significantly enhance both computational accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism centers around intelligently adjusting quantum loop parameters to guide the simulation process, resulting in improved fidelity and reduced computational cost. The research explores the potential of this approach in various quantum simulation scenarios and highlights its advantages over existing methods. The paper details the framework's design, mathematical foundations, and experimental validation, demonstrating its effectiveness in modeling complex quantum phenomena.

title: Dynamic Geometry Adjustment Adaptive Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic geometry complexity adjustment model for model parameter optimization. Traditional model parameter optimization methods often rely on manual tuning or fixed parameter sets, which can be inefficient and may not always achieve optimal performance. This work proposes a dynamically adjusted model parameter optimization strategy that adapts to the input data's geometric complexity, automatically refining the model's parameters to achieve superior performance. The model utilizes a geometric complexity assessment to intelligently adjust parameters, leading to a more robust and adaptable optimization process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its ability to efficiently and effectively optimize model performance across a range of scenarios.

title: High-Order Matrix Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel learning method for matrices based on high-order matrix dynamic plasticity. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the parameters of a matrix through a self-adaptive mechanism, enhancing generalization ability and efficiency. Traditional matrix learning often relies on fixed parameters, while high-order matrix learning offers the ability to dynamically adjust parameters. This approach aims to improve learning efficiency and generalization performance. The study demonstrates the effectiveness of this method through extensive experiments.
